Cybersecurity represents one of our most important near-term opportunities. As each new generation of AI models grows more capable of finding and exploiting vulnerabilities, we expect that defending enterprise networks and critical infrastructure will increasingly require frontier models. At the same time, the diffusion of AI is expanding the threat surface, as organizations deploy agents and autonomous capabilities at an accelerating pace. Our leadership in coding has allowed us to advance Claude’s cybersecurity capabilities and build products that help enterprises secure their most critical infrastructure. For example, Claude Security can continuously scan customers’ codebases, triage vulnerabilities, and write fixes. We also recently launched OSS Scanner, which extends some of these capabilities to the open-source projects that enterprise software is built on. Through our trusted-access programs, vetted cyberdefenders can also use our most capable models for security operations, incident response, and authorized penetration testing, shifting security to a continuous protection model.
We expect other sectors to follow as Claude’s frontier capabilities extend beyond current markets to open entirely new ones, reaching domains such as robotics, advanced manufacturing, and logistics, and accelerating progress in scientific research, including drug discovery and materials science.
For example, in the life sciences sector, where annual global pharmaceutical spend is expected to exceed $2 trillion in 2026,14 Claude is used in drug discovery and development by our customers, our biotechnology partners, and our own researchers. We are also extending Claude into robotics, where our Model Hardware Standard enables AI agents to operate lab and manufacturing equipment such as microscopes, liquid handlers, and off-the-shelf robotic arms.

text:
The Importance of Safety and Ethical Behavior
While the potential benefits of AI are extraordinary, its rapid advancement will impact the economy and society in ways that could create significant disruption, particularly if these technologies are not developed and deployed responsibly. For example, bad actors have already conducted high-profile cyberattacks using frontier model capabilities to discover vulnerabilities, generate malware, and evade detection tools; other risks associated with misuse, including in the domain of biology, could result in even greater harm. Frontier models deployed at scale also have the potential to concentrate power and wealth both within and between countries in ways that could erode trust, harm society, and destabilize the geopolitical order. Misaligned models could corrupt institutional decision-making or cause large-scale harm through autonomous actions that are not visible or understandable to their users and operators. We believe that companies at the frontier must invest in safety and alignment to help ensure the responsible diffusion of this technology. We also believe that safety, alignment, and ethical behavior resonate particularly strongly with enterprises, where rigorous safeguards, predictable model behavior, and demonstrable accountability have become decisive criteria in selecting a partner for mission-critical workloads.

text:
Mission and Focus
Anthropic was founded in 2021 by a team of researchers responsible for many of the breakthroughs that define frontier intelligence. They share a conviction that safety must be a foundational principle for building Powerful AI. We have a corporate structure consistent with that objective, incorporating as a Delaware PBC and implementing the LTBT with an explicit mandate to advance our mission. Further, we publish safety methodologies, model evaluations, and our Responsible Scaling Policy because we believe transparency is a prerequisite for trust, and trust is a prerequisite for the responsible deployment of frontier models at scale.
IQVIA Institute for Human Data Science, Global Medicine Use Trends 2026, February 2026.
Every employee at Anthropic works towards the same mission, and that mission guides every decision—from model architectures, to product strategy, to partnership terms, and to how we direct research and compute. We do not pursue projects based on commercial opportunity or research novelty alone; our efforts must advance our mission. When difficult tradeoffs arise between commercial gain and safety or trust, we have a clear answer. For example, in April 2026, we initially released our frontier model, Mythos, as a gated research preview through Project Glasswing, available to select organizations for cybersecurity applications, rather than making it broadly available at launch due to its advanced capabilities in cyber vulnerability discovery. We believe this clarity of mission reduces friction, accelerates decision-making, and fosters a culture where safety and capability are pursued in tandem.

text:
Talent and Culture
Talent is one of our most important advantages, because technology, capital, product, and distribution all flow from superior talent. Talent density matters more than talent mass. Brilliant people are inspired and motivated when surrounded by equally brilliant colleagues, creating an environment that attracts more exceptional people. This talent can leverage Claude to maximize each individual’s impact.
We believe we have assembled the deepest concentration of AI research talent in the world, including many of the researchers who pioneered the techniques that underlie modern LLMs. Our founding team originated several foundational advances in AI, including Scaling Laws, GPT-2 and GPT-3, RLHF, and mechanistic interpretability. Our conviction that safety and capability must advance together helps us attract and retain world-class talent, including researchers and engineers. For example, we have experienced approximately 1% regrettable attrition of our employee base overall in the TTM period ended September 30, 2026.
We maintain a commitment to open internal collaboration and truth seeking, which is underpinned by our low-ego, high-impact, and mission-aligned culture. Researchers share results openly, and colleagues critique and redirect in real time. When multiple teams pursue parallel approaches, the norm is to rigorously evaluate which approach is demonstrating stronger and more aligned results. This collaborative dynamic is difficult to replicate because it requires both the foundation of trust we have built from the earliest days of our organization and a relentless commitment to preserving such trust. That trust manifests in ways that are uncommon at our scale: teams that consistently pull in the same direction rather than at cross-purposes.
We believe our culture has driven our talent density as we have scaled.

location: BUSINESS > Our Core Advantages > Frontier and Safety Research
text:
Frontier and Safety Research
Our frontier model leadership is a direct product of our talent density. We believe our researchers have consistently pushed the boundaries of intelligence, capability, and reliability further than bigger teams or those with larger budgets. Claude is widely recognized for its performance on real-world tasks across industries, including coding, medicine, law, science, and mathematics.
Our approach to research provides key advantages to our business:
•Our Model Research and Compute Performance Are Co-designed from the Start. Architectural decisions are made with compute efficiency in mind from day one. Our model architecture and inference infrastructure are designed in a single unified process. AI researchers and inference infrastructure engineers share planning cycles, reporting lines, and performance targets. This approach enables us to develop model versions that are both more capable and more efficient compared to prior versions.
•Our Pre-training Process Is Engineered for Capital Efficiency. We focus on a clear pipeline for developing model improvements to architecture, training methodology, and data. These are tested at a smaller scale before they consume significant compute. The bar for inclusion in a frontier training run is high and strictly evidence-based: we require demonstration that a given improvement holds as models increase in size, not merely that it performs well at reduced scale. Frontier training runs are planned, scheduled capital deployments with known inputs and rigorous inclusion criteria. The result is a repeatable process for converting research investment into capability gains, while managing the risks inherent to frontier training runs.
•Our Post-training Investment Is Purpose-Built for Agentic Capabilities. Post-training has grown from a finishing step into a major research investment, reflecting the market shift from assistants to agents. This is where our models hone their ability to write code, use tools, follow instructions, and operate software on a user’s behalf. We train against complete, realistic tasks whose complexity reflects real professional work.
title: US-PROSPECTUS (S-1/A, preliminary) | BUSINESS > Our Core Advantages > Frontier and Safety Research

location: BUSINESS > Our Core Advantages > Frontier and Safety Research
text: •Our Safety Research Is a Commercial Benefit. As models take on agentic roles with access to critical business systems, trust and reliability are paramount. And as capabilities increase, the ability to operate safely becomes one of the key determining factors for commercial viability. Models that are well-aligned are better at following a user’s instructions—for example, they avoid taking potentially destructive actions without fully understanding user intent. They are also more robust against attacks such as prompt injection, where malicious actors attempt to hijack the model by feeding it illicit instructions. Our work on alignment, interpretability research, safeguards, and red-teaming, as well as the use of external reviewers who can assess our safety practices, helps us create safer, more reliable models, and therefore positions us to meet our customers’ rigorous requirements. Safety and capability research are integrated, which enables us to deliver the trust and performance required for enterprise workflows.

location: BUSINESS > Our Core Advantages > Our Approach to Compute
text:
Our Approach to Compute
Our approach to compute starts with training models that are designed to be more capable and run more efficiently on any given type of compute.
Our ability to build more capable models and serve them more efficiently reflects the compounding returns of an iterative cycle between our pre-training, post-training, and inference research, all of which is enabled by our fungible compute pool. Pre- and post-training research produces proprietary compute multipliers that make our models more capable. Research and inference engineering drive sustained reductions in the compute required to serve those models.
In addition to enabling more capable and efficient models, our multi-chip compute architecture across AWS Trainium, Google TPUs, NVIDIA GPUs, and AMD GPUs allows us to orchestrate workloads to optimize for price and performance. We have years of experience effectively training and running our models across multiple chip families, which we believe is differentiated and difficult to replicate. This foundation, paired with Claude’s increasing understanding of chip and model architectures, allows us to onboard new chip platforms in a fraction of the time this once required.
Our compute pool is fungible by design. We have made substantial engineering investments to build the internal orchestration, scheduling, and capacity management systems that allow accelerator capacity, regardless of provider, chip architecture, or physical location, to be directed across workloads. The same infrastructure that serves customer workloads is also directed to research, model development, and internal usage of Claude. These systems manage the underlying hardware as a unified capacity pool, monitor utilization and demand across that pool, and direct compute to wherever it is expected to be most productive at any given time.
Our multi-chip compute approach provides us with substantially greater chip access than relying on one platform and enables us to opportunistically capture the price-performance benefits of each chip family and generation. Securing this access requires significant advance commitment. Given the long lead times between contracting for compute and that compute becoming available to serve workloads, we secure compute well in advance of anticipated demand. In some cases, we may also make payments in advance of the delivery of the equipment or infrastructure. We anticipate making significant investments for the foreseeable future, including in compute and infrastructure, to ensure we have the technological resources to maintain and expand our position at the frontier of AI.

Enterprise Strategy
Our enterprise strategy aligns with our mission. We build our most capable models for the problems that demand the highest intelligence. That same intelligence is also applied efficiently to everyday work—calibrating effort to the difficulty of each task and routing workloads to the models within our model family that are best suited for them. As a result, our customers around the world are adopting Claude across a broad range of work, from routine knowledge tasks to their most important problems. Today, Claude is deployed for knowledge work across major industries, including financial services, insurance, healthcare, life sciences, law, education, retail and commerce, telecommunications, professional services, technology, and cybersecurity. Beyond practical enterprise challenges, Claude is also being applied to pressing global problems in scientific research, drug discovery, education, and climate analysis.
We have built our models, platform, and applications for usefulness in production environments instead of benchmark performance. This distinction matters, as many AI systems prove difficult to implement and fail to deliver the expected value in complex enterprise environments, where governance and security concerns remain among the top barriers to adoption.
Our applications, such as Claude Code and Claude Cowork, multiply the impact of employees. Over time, our applications have become more capable and are now frequently being used to conduct long-running autonomous work alongside employees. Organizations also integrate Claude as the intelligence that powers and transforms internal business processes. In addition, the Claude Platform is used as the foundation for enterprises building AI-native products.
As enterprise customers integrate Claude into increasingly complex workflows, they surface the use cases and requirements that shape our roadmap. They also provide feedback that allows us to continuously improve our models, platform, and applications as well as develop new solutions to advance their AI adoption.

location: BUSINESS > Our Core Advantages > Enterprise Strategy
text: With each model and product advancement, Claude is able to address more valuable use cases, deepening its impact for existing customers while lowering the adoption threshold for new ones. When a model crosses the capability, reliability, and trust threshold required for a category of work, adoption in that category generally moves quickly from experimentation into production. Coding was the first such category: within roughly a year, Claude progressed from suggesting individual lines of code to operating fleets of agents working autonomously across production codebases. Cybersecurity is following a similar curve, with Claude’s performance on ExploitBench, a benchmark developed by Carnegie Mellon researchers that evaluates AI models’ ability to exploit software vulnerabilities, increasing from 40% with Opus 4.8, to 78% with Mythos 5, and to 91% with Opus 5.5 over a period of approximately four months. Cyberdefenders are now identifying and patching vulnerabilities at scale. We expect these improvements in model capabilities to unlock additional use cases. Claude Security and our recently launched OSS Scanner are early examples, providing the ability to scan codebases on a continuous basis and propose fixes before attackers find vulnerabilities.

location: BUSINESS > Claude as a Virtual Collaborator
text:
We believe we have reached an inflection point where Claude and other systems can function as genuine collaborators in professional work. They quickly complete substantive tasks that might otherwise occupy a skilled professional for several hours, a full day, or longer. These systems are also becoming increasingly capable of performing tasks that were previously too difficult or costly to complete or surfacing original insights and analyses.
We refer to these AI systems that work alongside humans to perform complex, multi-step work at professional levels as Virtual Collaborators. Virtual Collaborators carry the access rights, system connections, and context that their organizations grant them, which allows them to function more accurately and reliably. They can navigate and use internal tools and execute workflows that span multiple steps that require sustained reasoning. Virtual Collaborators are AI designed to be embedded where work gets done, and our aim is to continue extending them to knowledge workers globally, a population that is estimated to exceed one billion in 2028.15
title: US-PROSPECTUS (S-1/A, preliminary) | BUSINESS > Claude as a Virtual Collaborator

location: BUSINESS > Claude as a Virtual Collaborator > Claude Code
text:
Claude Code
The clearest manifestation of Virtual Collaborators today is Claude Code, our coding agent and the product we believe has most concretely defined what autonomous work at the frontier looks like. Claude Code shifted the market’s understanding of what frontier models could do in collaboration with software developers: the model suggests the next line of code and goes further by planning, writing, testing, and debugging—a process that results in production-grade code. Within months of its release, autonomous coding became the reference point for measuring the progress of frontier intelligence. For enterprise use cases, we believe the launch of Claude Code was comparable in its impact to the introduction of the first widely adopted conversational AI assistants. What makes Claude Code a Virtual Collaborator is its sustained reasoning, a harness that translates intent into actions, an execution environment that maintains a persistent state whether on a developer’s machine or in a sandboxed cloud environment, integration with existing tools and systems, and a user-friendly interface. Its uses are highly varied and often surprising: for example, NASA engineers used Claude Code to plan and write navigation commands for the Mars Perseverance rover, resulting in the first AI-planned drive on Mars.
Software developers are powerful advocates for Claude—they understand how systems work, have credibility evaluating technical tools, and often serve as internal champions for adopting new technologies. Winning their trust creates a foundation for broader diffusion of Virtual Collaborators across enterprise workforces. We are already seeing this pattern play out with non-technical teams increasingly adopting Claude Code and Claude Cowork to manage their own workflows.

Claude Cowork

All digital work is ultimately an expression of code, and Claude’s mastery of it powers Virtual Collaborators capable of handling complex work far beyond software development. Claude Cowork extends the agentic architecture of Claude Code to knowledge workers broadly by translating a user’s intent into completed work, autonomously reading files, navigating applications, and executing multi-step workflows on a user’s desktop while the underlying code is abstracted away. By extending beyond Claude Code with applications purpose-built for specific professions and industry verticals, we accelerate Claude’s diffusion into new categories of knowledge work and deepen our presence across the enterprise. As of September 30, 2026, adoption of Claude Cowork, which we made available as a research preview in January 2026, outpaced the adoption Claude Code achieved at the equivalent point following its research preview release in February 2025. In September 2026, we began merging Claude Cowork and Claude.ai, bringing agentic and conversational work into a unified application. Users can now move from a simple question to complex, multi-step tasks in the same conversation.

Extending Virtual Collaborators
We believe the trajectory for Virtual Collaborators is clear and accelerating. Each generation of Claude models has expanded along multiple dimensions: the depth and rigor of their reasoning, the duration and autonomy of the work they can sustain, the complexity of tasks they can complete, and the volume of useful output they can produce. Capability evaluations and benchmarking have shown substantial improvements across Claude model versions in the duration and complexity of tasks that can be completed reliably, with more recent model versions demonstrating particularly significant advances.
We are building towards a world where Claude can be given open-ended tasks lasting hours, days, or weeks, and then execute them autonomously with the judgment and initiative of a brilliant colleague. Ultimately, millions of Virtual Collaborators can run in parallel, each working independently on unrelated problems or collaborating seamlessly to achieve a shared objective. The result is something without historical precedent: what we refer to as a country of geniuses in a data center, available to every organization and sector of the economy.

location: BUSINESS > Claude is the Partner of Choice for Enterprises > Claude Platform—A Composable System for Building AI Solutions
text:
Claude Platform—A Composable System for Building AI Solutions
We seek to bring Claude to every corner of the economy at whatever level of autonomy each task demands, from a single suggestion to an agent that runs independently for hours. Achieving this goal requires more than a capable model. The most demanding deployments need intelligence that is reliable, connectable, and deployable within the specific data environments, regulatory constraints, and workflow patterns of each organization. Intelligence is one limiting factor, but so are connectors that do not yet exist, governance frameworks that are not yet written, and orchestration logic that needs to be built from scratch. Our platform seeks to close these gaps, and we believe the breadth and speed with which we have done so are primary reasons customers build on Claude.
Our platform provides our customers with direct access to the primitives to build, deploy, and scale AI-native applications. At the foundation are model capabilities that make Claude’s autonomy possible: native tool use, computer use for desktop control, memory, and extended thinking. Long context and low-latency model variants make that action sustainable: for example, an agent could hold an entire codebase, a full data room, or hours of accumulated task state in working memory and iterate fast enough that autonomy persists rather than stalls. Above these sit composition primitives such as our Agent Software Development Kit (“SDK”), Claude Managed Agents, Agent Skills, multi-agent orchestration, and the Model Context Protocol (“MCP”) for universal connectivity to enterprise data and tools. Together, these assemble into complex production workflows.
These building blocks are composable and interoperable. The same primitives that power a coding agent also power a research agent, a financial analyst agent, or a compliance-review agent. While these agents have different connectors and agent skills, they have the same SDK, protocol, and orchestration framework. That composability is one of the reasons our customer base spans industries and why customer expansion can happen seamlessly across additional use cases without significant integration work.

A Platform Customers Build Their Businesses On
Customers of all sizes and across every major industry have adopted Claude. Fortune 500 companies, including American International Group, Inc. and Bristol Myers Squibb, rely on Claude for mission-critical workflows. Research institutions, such as the Garvan Institute of Medical Research, Gladstone Institutes, and the University of California, San Francisco, are applying Claude to some of the world’s hardest scientific problems. In addition, prosumers around the world use Claude as a daily tool.
As enterprises adopt our platform and applications, we become deeply embedded in their businesses over time. Software developers build applications and internal tools on our platform, and they encode their workflows and institutional knowledge into Claude-powered agents. Organizations integrate Claude into essential business processes. Each additional integration deepens the relationship and increases the value customers derive from the platform. This dynamic extends beyond our direct customers. Leading companies such as Legora and Salesforce have built AI-powered products on Claude that reach millions of end users. This reach can increase awareness of Claude, which we believe drives adoption far beyond our direct customer base. When such end users experience Claude, it can build preference and familiarity that travel with users across roles and organizations.
The result is an ecosystem where we build on our own platform and applications, our customers build on us, our partners build on us, and their end users experience Claude across surfaces, creating the kind of deep workflow integration that makes our platform and applications increasingly central to how organizations operate. We believe the revenue we generate today does not reflect the full economic value Claude creates for our customers—not just for the organizations that build on us, but for the people whose work, learning, and creativity are expanded by the intelligence and skills they gain through Claude. We believe that there is substantial opportunity ahead as Claude’s capabilities, adoption, and integration into critical workflows continue to grow.

Our distribution strategy is built around one objective: getting Claude’s intelligence in the hands of every enterprise, team, and individual that can benefit from it. A core driver of Claude’s diffusion is its intelligence— as Claude’s capabilities advance, value to customers expands, and that value drives greater adoption. Our role is also to ensure that intelligence is accessible, and we do that in the following ways: through our composable platform and applications that meet customers where they are, through our go-to-market and Applied AI teams directly, and through partnerships that extend our reach at scale.
Intelligence-Led Growth. Our platform and applications are the primary mechanism through which Claude’s intelligence reaches users. As users begin building, brainstorming, and problem-solving with Claude, they quickly come to rely on it as a trusted partner in their work. As Claude takes on more of their work, people experience firsthand what frontier intelligence makes possible and expand their usage significantly. This pattern repeats across organizations: prosumers become internal champions, teams expand their use of Claude, and what begins as a single workflow grows into something that impacts how an entire organization operates.
Direct Teams. This organic adoption is complemented and enhanced through our direct go-to-market teams who help scale Claude to organizations with complex workflows and business processes. By the time our direct teams engage a customer, Claude is often already in use. Our go-to-market teams use this organic momentum to build executive sponsorship and drive enterprise-wide adoption.
Applied AI Teams. Our Applied AI teams embed more deeply with select customers, building solutions that make it easier for organizations to benefit from Claude’s intelligence. They work with enterprises to design and deploy custom solutions, specialized workflows, and domain-specific implementations tailored to the customer’s own requirements. This work drives deeper adoption within individual customers and generates the feedback and information from users that help to shape our platform and product roadmap. Our direct and Applied AI teams work together as a hybrid sales and engineering function, organized by geography and then by industry so that they bring domain expertise to each customer.
Partnerships. We complement our direct efforts through distribution partnerships that place Claude inside customers’ existing technology stacks.

location: BUSINESS > Our Models, Platform, and Applications > The Claude Model Family
text:
The Claude Model Family
The Claude model family is currently composed of four model classes: Mythos (including Fable), Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku. Our model classes can be used individually for certain tasks or in combination with one another. They offer broad flexibility to choose the ideal performance, cost, and speed for each use case. All models support text, code, and multimodal inputs.
•Mythos (including Fable). Our most capable model class, delivering frontier performance across all domains and solving problems AI has not reliably handled before, especially in coding and long-running agentic tasks. Given its advanced capabilities in sensitive areas like software vulnerability discovery and biology, we deploy this underlying model in two distinct configurations. Fable is generally available and runs with our production safeguards, which block or limit performance on certain sensitive topics, including by routing requests to a less capable Claude model. Mythos runs with safeguards calibrated for vetted organizations and individuals doing cybersecurity and life sciences work, and is available through our trusted-access programs, including our Cyber Verification Program. We first made the class available in April 2026 as Claude Mythos Preview through Project Glasswing. We made Fable 5 generally available and offered Mythos 5 to Project Glasswing participants in June 2026, released Mythos 5.1 and Fable 5.1 in September 2026, and released Mythos 5.2 and Fable 5.2 in November 2026.
•Opus. Our powerful workhorse model class for reasoning-intensive tasks. Our most recent Opus release, Opus 5.5, is designed to serve as the enterprise daily driver, powering agents that run projects end to end and advancing capabilities across agentic coding, computer use, and knowledge work. Opus models consistently rank among leading models on key industry benchmarks.
•Sonnet. Our versatile model class for everyday tasks, providing a balance of performance, cost, and speed for the widest set of general-purpose use cases, including high-volume sub-agents in multi-agent orchestration setups.
•Haiku. Our lowest-cost and fastest model class. Haiku models are designed for high-volume workloads like customer service agents and large-scale document processing.

location: BUSINESS > Our Models, Platform, and Applications > The Claude Platform
text:
The Claude Platform
Customers choose Claude for more than the models. The Claude Platform lets developers and businesses build, manage, and deploy agentic AI applications on infrastructure with high reliability, security, and availability.
Platform Features
Platform features enable developers to customize their usage of Claude, including:
•Extended Thinking. Claude can perform additional internal reasoning before producing a final response, working through complex, multi-step problems to improve response quality on tasks like analysis, math, and coding.
•Adaptive Thinking. Claude automatically calibrates whether a given request calls for extended reasoning and how much reasoning to apply—so developers get the benefits of extended reasoning without configuring reasoning levels request by request.
•Effort Controls. Developers can specify an effort level on each request to guide how much reasoning Claude applies, allowing them to balance response quality against cost and latency.
•Tool Use. Claude can natively call external functions and APIs throughout a conversation, with support for parallel execution and interleaved thinking between tool calls. The search tool loads only the tools required for a given task on demand, which can reduce token overhead compared to loading full tool libraries upfront.
•Long Context. Claude supports large context windows and maintains its strong performance even as inputs grow, meaning that developers can include entire codebases, large document sets, or long agent histories in a single request.
•Structured Outputs. Developers can constrain Claude’s responses to a specified schema, such as valid JSON (JavaScript Object Notation), so results integrate reliably with downstream systems and application code with less additional parsing or validation.
•Code Execution. A sandboxed execution environment where Claude can write, run, and iterate on code within an agent loop, which is foundational for data analysis and automation workflows. This environment lets Claude call tools and process large volumes of data more efficiently and run the scripts packaged in Agent Skills.
•Web Search. A native tool giving Claude access to real-time web information, enabling grounded, citation-aware responses in production applications.
•Files API. Allows developers to upload documents once and reference them across multiple sessions, simplifying workflows that depend on persistent documents.
Context Management
Developers can connect context to Claude for their agents and applications using context primitives.
title: US-PROSPECTUS (S-1/A, preliminary) | BUSINESS > Our Models, Platform, and Applications > The Claude Platform

location: BUSINESS > Our Models, Platform, and Applications > The Claude Platform
text:
•Model Context Protocol. MCP is an open standard we introduced in November 2024 and donated to the Linux Foundation’s Agentic AI Foundation in December 2025. MCP defines a universal interface through which Claude, as well as other AI tools, can connect to enterprise data sources, tools, and workflows. Claude Platform’s native MCP connector handles connection management, tool discovery, and error handling automatically.
•Agent Skills. A modular framework that lets organizations encode repeatable tasks, workflows, and domain expertise into reusable packages, or skills, that Claude loads on demand. We provide pre-built skills for common formats like Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and PDF, while custom skills can capture anything from engineering standards and regulatory processes to proprietary toolchains. These skills turn institutional knowledge into agent capabilities.
•Model Hardware Standard. Currently in research preview, our Model Hardware Standard enables AI agents to find, understand, and safely operate lab and manufacturing equipment such as microscopes, liquid handlers, and off-the-shelf robotic arms. Our Model Hardware Standard is model-agnostic and lets any agent harness reach devices with a programmable interface through standard protocols such as MCP.
Infrastructure
The Claude Platform offers high reliability and availability for enterprise-grade agentic workloads. Customers building on Claude need the model served dependably wherever they operate, they need it to run efficiently at scale and speed, and they need the tooling that allows a model to work on its own. We operate that infrastructure so our customers do not have to build and maintain it themselves.
•Availability. The Claude Platform is available directly from Anthropic and through the major cloud providers, including AWS, GCP, and Azure. Feature availability varies by deployment.
•Cost, Speed, and Scale. Developers can tune how Claude runs to fit the performance and economics of each workload:
◦Prompt Caching. Large, reused prompt components can be cached for up to one hour, reducing cost by up to approximately 97% and latency by approximately 60% for long prompts, compared with processing the same requests without caching.
◦Batch Processing. Enables high-volume asynchronous processing at reduced cost.
◦Fast Mode. Delivers lower-latency responses for latency-sensitive and interactive applications where speed is critical.
Harnesses
title: US-PROSPECTUS (S-1/A, preliminary) | BUSINESS > Our Models, Platform, and Applications > The Claude Platform

location: BUSINESS > Our Models, Platform, and Applications > The Claude Platform
text:
A model alone is not an agent. Running one reliably in production is challenging, because agents must survive crashes and interruptions, act on systems with scoped and auditable credentials, and scale across variable workloads. Autonomous operation requires a harness, which provides the secure environment, credentials, memory, and orchestration loop a model needs to plan, call tools, verify its work, and complete a task safely on its own. Building and operating that infrastructure is specialized, continuous work that, until recently, each customer had to take on themselves. We offer two ways to run a harness on the Claude Platform:
•Agent SDK. This solution makes the same production-grade harness that powers Claude Code available to all developers, to run on their own compute. It provides built-in context management, session handling, multi-agent coordination, and prompt optimization, so customers can build and run sophisticated agents on their own infrastructure in a fraction of the time otherwise required.
•Claude Managed Agents. An out-of-the-box solution in which we operate the harness on our customers’ behalf, on Anthropic-managed compute. We host the sandboxes, store the credentials, maintain the memory, and run the agent loop; customers define their agent’s tasks, tools, and guardrails. When a new model becomes available, customers do not need to rebuild their agent loop.

text:
Direct Applications and Integrations
Our platform primitives and models are the foundation for all of our products and support a wide range of use cases, from coding agents to specialized products in life sciences, finance, security, and more. Paired with our deep understanding of current and future capabilities of our models, this foundation allows us to rapidly deliver products that unlock value across many user types and workflows.
•Claude Code. A coding agent, available as a terminal tool, desktop app, web interface, and mobile app, with native integrations for GitHub and popular IDEs (Integrated Development Environments). Claude Code handles multi-step software development tasks—planning, writing, editing, testing, debugging, and committing code—across large codebases with sustained context and supports parallel agent sessions, so a single developer can keep multiple tasks moving at once.
•Claude Cowork. A knowledge work agent on desktop, web, and mobile, built on Claude Code’s agentic architecture. Users describe a task in plain language and Claude breaks it into steps and completes them across local files, connected apps, Chrome, and the desktop itself, clicking and typing through native applications when no integration exists. It returns finished documents, spreadsheets, presentations, and organized folders, with no terminal or code required. An open-source plugin system lets users install or build packages bundling skills, data connectors, and workflows.
•Claude.ai. Our flagship conversational product, available on desktop, web, and mobile. Claude.ai is the broadest entry point to Claude, available to enterprises, teams, and individuals, offering access across our Claude model family with support for file uploads, projects for persistent context across conversations, memory, web search, and artifacts for real-time code and document rendering. Claude.ai delivers top-of-funnel demand generation for enterprise adoption. In September 2026, we began merging Claude Cowork and Claude.ai into a unified application, such that any request is automatically handled using the appropriate tools, drawing on Claude Cowork’s capabilities.
•Claude Security. A defensive cybersecurity product, available in public beta to Claude Enterprise customers, that puts frontier vulnerability detection and patching into the hands of security teams. Claude Security reasons about code the way a security researcher does, tracing data flows and examining how components interact across a codebase to uncover complex, context-dependent vulnerabilities that pattern-based scanners can miss. Each finding is surfaced with a confidence rating, severity assessment, and reproduction steps. Users can move directly into Claude Code to review and apply the proposed patch, compressing the time from scan to fix.
title: US-PROSPECTUS (S-1/A, preliminary) | BUSINESS > Our Models, Platform, and Applications > Direct Applications and Integrations

location: BUSINESS > Our Models, Platform, and Applications > Direct Applications and Integrations
text:
•Claude Tag. A collaborative agent that works alongside teams in productivity tools like Slack, where users tag Claude into any channel or thread and delegate work in plain language. With the context of the surrounding conversation, enterprise software tools, shared documents, and channel-scoped memory, Claude returns answers, drafts, analyses, and pull requests directly in-thread, operating as an ambient teammate that knows when to proactively join the conversation. Claude Tag brings Claude into the multiplayer workflows where teams already coordinate, extending adoption from individuals to entire organizations.
•Claude Design. Enables users to create polished designs, prototypes, presentations, and other visual work through natural language conversation and direct editing. Claude Design extends our platform into visual and creative work, broadening the range of professional tasks for which designers, marketers, founders, and go-to-market professionals can utilize Claude.
•Claude Science. An AI workbench for scientific research that brings literature analysis, data processing, and manuscript preparation into a single desktop environment. Researchers describe an analysis in plain language, and Claude Science queries more than 60 scientific databases to complete it end to end. Claude Science executes computationally intensive workloads on a lab’s own machines, institutional computing clusters, or on-demand cloud resources, without requiring researchers to manage the underlying infrastructure. It returns publication-ready figures and manuscripts—with natively rendered scientific outputs, fully reproducible code, agent-powered verification, and traceable results. Claude Science extends Claude into scientific research, putting frontier capabilities directly in the hands of researchers working on some of the world’s hardest problems.
Customers can access each of these products through our Claude Enterprise offering. Claude Enterprise provides security and compliance controls, including SAML (Security Assertion Markup Language)-based single sign-on with SCIM (System for Cross-domain Identity Management) provisioning, role-based access controls, audit logging, a Compliance API, and configurations designed to support Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (“HIPAA”) compliance for healthcare and regulated-data workloads—alongside a centralized administrative console for IT oversight, cost visibility, and controls.

location: BUSINESS > Our Models, Platform, and Applications > Direct Applications and Integrations
text: Customers in regulated industries and beyond use our most capable models for sensitive work. These customers must keep their data private, and we must be able to detect misuse. In September 2026, we announced Enterprise Frontier Safeguards, which is designed to address both needs. The activity data we use for automated safety monitoring is stored in the customer’s own cloud account, under the customer’s encryption keys and access controls. Our automated systems review recent activity for signs of serious misuse and send alerts of such misuse directly to the customer’s security team. No review by Anthropic employees is required. We developed Enterprise Frontier Safeguards with more than 100 customers in industries including financial services, healthcare, and the public sector. We are rolling out this feature in phases and, until the completion of the rollout, eligible customers receive zero data retention on Fable 5, Fable 5.1, and Fable 5.2, meaning that, except where needed to comply with applicable law or combat misuse or harm, we do not store their inputs or outputs after we process a request.

text:
Vertical Solutions
Beyond our horizontal platform and applications, we are building vertical solutions in industries where domain specificity and regulatory requirements make general-purpose tools insufficient. Our vertical solutions arrive purpose-built and are embedded with domain knowledge, controls designed to support industry-specific compliance requirements, and pre-configured data integrations that reduce time-to-value. Our vertical solutions are delivered through a range of channels, including our Claude Enterprise and Team plans, domain-specific connectors and plugins available on our individual subscription plans, Claude Platform, and, in the case of Claude for Education, institution-wide agreements. To date, we have launched seven vertical solutions:
•Claude for Financial Services. Provides financial professionals with pre-built, customizable AI agents for common finance workflows, such as drafting pitch books, reviewing earnings, running know-your-customer screenings, and conducting financial analysis. Claude for Financial Services plugs directly into the data sources financial firms already use (e.g., market data, data warehouses) and runs inside the tools financial professionals utilize—such as Excel, PowerPoint, Word, Outlook, and Claude’s own apps.
•Claude for Financial Advisors. Provides financial advisors and wealth management firms with pre-built, customizable workflows for common advisory tasks, such as preparing for client meetings, drafting follow-ups, reviewing portfolio rebalances, and preparing estate and tax briefs. Claude for Financial Advisors plugs directly into the systems advisors already use (e.g., custodial platforms, portfolio management and financial planning tools, and customer relationship management software), with advisor review built into each workflow to help firms meet their compliance requirements.
•Claude for Healthcare. Gives providers, payers, and health technology companies frontier models with domain intelligence across clinical reasoning, medical coding, and long-horizon agentic operations, as well as tools designed to support HIPAA compliance for medical and operational workflows. Claude for Healthcare also connects to industry systems including the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services Coverage Database, ICD-10, and National Provider Identifier (NPI) Registry, with agent skills for Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) development and prior authorization reviews.
•Claude for Life Sciences. Provides computational biologists, bioinformaticians, clinical trial managers, and regulatory affairs specialists with domain intelligence built into frontier models across organic chemistry, structural biology, lab protocols, and bioinformatics pipelines. Claude for Life Sciences supports work across the development chain, from early discovery and preclinical research through clinical trial operations and regulatory submissions. Claude plugs directly into the tools and databases researchers already use, such as electronic lab notebooks, data repositories, and scientific literature.

location: BUSINESS > Our Infrastructure > Multi-Chip Compute Approach
text:
Multi-Chip Compute Approach
We have built a deliberate and diversified compute sourcing strategy across multiple chip platforms that provides the following distinct advantages:
•We can secure compute from multiple providers rather than being constrained by any single provider.
•We can select chips based on the best price-performance and efficiency characteristics for each workload, benefiting from the differentiated strengths of each platform.
•We maintain collaborative relationships with each of our providers, and we influence roadmaps and features of future chip generations. Our chip platforms include:
◦AWS Trainium. Our strategic collaboration with Amazon provides us with access to accelerators, including custom-designed Trainium chips, and compute infrastructure, as well as the opportunity to influence future generations of Trainium chips.
◦Google TPUs. Our partnerships with Google and Broadcom provide us with access to compute capacity powered by Google TPUs across multiple generations of the TPU platform.
◦NVIDIA GPUs. Our strategic partnership with NVIDIA, together with our arrangements with Microsoft, SpaceXAI, Nscale, Lambda, and other cloud providers, provides us with access to compute capacity powered by NVIDIA GPUs, including NVIDIA Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin GPU systems, as well as the opportunity to collaborate directly with NVIDIA on design and engineering to optimize future NVIDIA hardware for our workload profile.
◦AMD GPUs. Our relationship with AMD, together with our arrangements with approved manufacturers of AMD-based Helios rack-scale systems and third-party service providers, provides us with access to compute capacity powered by AMD Instinct™ GPUs, including AMD Instinct™ MI450 Series GPUs, as well as the opportunity to collaborate directly with AMD through a multi-year engineering collaboration.
•We can onboard new chip platforms in a fraction of the time it once took. Historically, bringing a new chip platform into production required intense engineering effort over many months. By leveraging Claude, our engineering teams can now bring new chip platforms into production more quickly. This speed and efficiency also rely on the robust foundation we have already built across multiple chip families, including a proprietary orchestration layer designed to seamlessly test and measure performance against our actual workloads. As a result, we are able to adopt new accelerators as they become available, expanding our access to compute capacity while reducing our dependence on any single hardware provider.
See the section titled “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations —Liquidity and Capital Resources—Contractual Obligations—Infrastructure Service Arrangements” for more information regarding the terms of these arrangements.
title: US-PROSPECTUS (S-1/A, preliminary) | BUSINESS > Our Infrastructure > Multi-Chip Compute Approach

location: BUSINESS > Our Infrastructure > Our Data Center Strategy
text:
Our Data Center Strategy
Historically, we purchased compute under fixed-time agreements. As our compute requirements have scaled, we have transitioned to a hybrid model in which, in addition to purchasing compute as a cloud service, we also procure specialized accelerators directly and operate this hardware in dedicated data center facilities leased and operated on our behalf, to our specification. We refer to this additional source of compute as Anthropic Direct. This transition is driven in part by the scale of our compute requirements as well as the potential long-term economic advantages of direct infrastructure leasing and hosting. Our first data center facility became operational this year.
Anthropic Direct also lets us separate our commitment to data center capacity from our commitment to the accelerators deployed inside it. Because data centers require longer lead times but represent a smaller fraction of total compute costs, this approach enables us to secure data center capacity early while deferring larger accelerator investments until our specific compute needs are more certain.
Our data center infrastructure strategy includes several contractual arrangements that, taken together, form a new source of compute to supplement the capacity we procure from our CSPs. Such arrangements include the following:
•Compute Infrastructure Equipment. We procure specialized accelerators and associated components, including CPUs and high-bandwidth memory, through master equipment leases, including the 2026 Lease Arrangement, pursuant to which we receive such hardware for deployment in dedicated data center facilities operated by others on our behalf. See the section titled “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations—Liquidity and Capital Resources— Contractual Obligations—Infrastructure Equipment Leases” for more information regarding the terms of these leases.
title: US-PROSPECTUS (S-1/A, preliminary) | BUSINESS > Our Infrastructure > Our Data Center Strategy

location: BUSINESS > Our Infrastructure > Our Data Center Strategy
text:
•Data Centers. In certain of our data center infrastructure arrangements, third-party partners procure the underlying real estate, power, and data center facilities, while we lease capacity in those facilities and contract with specialized third-party operators for ongoing facility management. For example, we have entered into a colocation and services agreement with Fluidstack USA I Inc. (“Fluidstack”), under which Fluidstack provides data center development and operations services to us. We have also executed data center leases directly and expect to do so increasingly over time. To secure certain data center development projects, which require significant capital commitments in advance of deployment, we have in some cases relied, and expect to continue to rely, on arrangements with financing sources or partners who guarantee the lease obligations to support the development of data center capacity that is expected to host such partner’s chips or computing infrastructure. Our ability to expand compute and infrastructure capacity through these arrangements in the future may depend on the continued willingness and ability of a limited number of CSPs, partners, and financing sources to enter into and perform under them.
•Electrical Power. Electrical power procurement requires separate arrangements with utility providers or, in some cases, development of behind-the-meter power generation capacity that supplies electricity directly to the facility rather than through the broader electric grid. Securing adequate power capacity for data center projects, whether through grid-connected or behind-the-meter arrangements, typically requires long lead times and significant financial commitments well in advance of when facilities become operational.
Our data center infrastructure projects are currently located primarily in the United States. As we continue to expand our global customer base and research operations, we are pursuing additional data center capacity internationally to support our full range of workloads.

text:
Organizations around the world rely on Claude. We serve a breadth of customers, from the largest enterprises to AI-native companies, government and research institutions, as well as prosumers.
As of September 30, 2026, our customers with $100,000 or more of revenue on a TTM basis included every company in the Fortune 10, over 50% of the Fortune 500, and over 30% of the Global 2000. Across industries, enterprises deploy Claude in mission-critical production workflows—for example, underwriting insurance policies, writing clinical reports for life-saving drugs, detecting and remediating cybersecurity threats, and analyzing portfolios for asset managers. In addition, leading AI-native companies build next-generation coding tools, design platforms, and productivity applications on Claude. Government and research institutions also apply Claude to work that ranges from materials science to energy security; mission-driven organizations use Claude to compress the expected timeline of scientific research, clinical workflows, and the delivery of public benefits.
Our customer base has grown rapidly in both the number and scale of customer relationships, with organizations expanding from initial use cases into enterprise-wide production deployments. As of September 30, 2026, we had more than 11,900 customers with $100,000 or more of revenue on a TTM basis, up from more than 950 as of September 30, 2025.
Our customers fall into two primary categories: enterprises and prosumers.

location: BUSINESS > Our Customers > Enterprises
text:
Enterprises
Our enterprise customers include a wide range of organizations deploying AI at scale, from AI-native startups building products to the world’s largest organizations that require enterprise-grade security, governance, and compliance before a single workflow impacts production. We serve this full spectrum from a single composable platform, providing frictionless access to our frontier models as well as the controls customers require, such as single sign-on, audit logging, data retention policies, role-based access controls, and native deployment within their existing cloud infrastructure.
Software developers remain a critical adoption force within enterprises: they are simultaneously customers, the architects of applications built on our platform, and the internal champions of organization-wide adoption. Software developers use Claude Code and the Claude Platform to write, debug, and ship production-quality code faster—architecting systems, implementing features, building agentic workflows, and resolving complex issues in hours that previously took days. These production deployments surface the governance, reliability, and integration requirements that only emerge under real enterprise load, which creates feedback that flows back into our roadmap and deepens our customer relationships with every release.

location: BUSINESS > Our Customers > Prosumers
text:
Prosumers
Knowledge workers, including researchers, developers, analysts, and writers, subscribe to our Claude Pro, Max, and Ultra plans to perform complex cognitive work, including drafting analyses, synthesizing research, writing and reviewing code, building financial models, and automating workflows. With Claude Cowork, non-technical prosumers build agentic workflows across their applications without writing code, accomplishing in minutes what previously required hours of manual effort.
Prosumers are some of our earliest adopters and often among our most discerning users. They test out capabilities within hours of the release of a model, push the latest version of Claude into use cases we may not have anticipated, and discover edge cases and failures that sharpen each successive version of a Claude model.
The adoption of Claude Code began with individual software developers who noticed the potential of autonomous coding agents before enterprise procurement teams had considered the category; Claude Code is now becoming the default choice inside many enterprise engineering organizations.
Prosumers serve as a powerful top-of-funnel engine—we have consistently seen that individuals who experience Claude’s value firsthand become advocates within their organizations, seeding adoption that accelerates from individual use to team-wide and ultimately organization-wide deployment.

location: BUSINESS > Our Customers > How Claude Drives Value for Customers
text:
How Claude Drives Value for Customers
Customers realize value from Claude in three primary ways: more productive employees, faster processes, and embedded intelligence in their products. These outcomes are different expressions of the same intelligence, each drawing on the same models and primitives.
More Productive Employees. Adoption most often begins here. An individual experiences the impact that a frontier model can have on their own output—for instance, hours of financial analysis or code review completed in minutes—and that conviction spreads from the first user to their team, and from one team to the entire company. This happens for Claude Code in software development; Claude Cowork delivers this for knowledge workers more broadly. Our Claude Enterprise plan provides the governance, security, and administration to support adoption of Claude at organizational scale.
Faster Processes. As adoption deepens, Claude stops being something employees consult and starts being something the organization runs on. As organizations encode more of their workflows into Claude—their data, systems, conventions, and prior work—the platform becomes more valuable for them. Claude can draw on that accumulated context to suggest the next workflow worth automating, reducing the effort required for each successive deployment.
Embedded Intelligence. At the deepest level, Claude moves from an operational advantage to a commercial one. Product teams build on the Claude Platform to embed frontier models into their own products, including customer-facing agents, AI-native features, and entirely new product lines that were not previously viable without AI capabilities. Claude is both a tool the organization uses and an ingredient in the value it delivers to its own customers.
Across all three dimensions, a significant share of expansion requires minimal to no new deployment at all. Each new version of a Claude model is designed to improve the performance of existing use cases: employees produce higher-quality work, encoded processes run with greater accuracy and reliability, and embedded products deliver more value to end users. As a result, customers can increase usage, utilize higher subscription tiers, and bring additional workflows onto the platform without a new sales cycle or procurement decision.

location: BUSINESS > Our Culture, Values, and Talent
text:
Anthropic was founded by a team of researchers who believe that the most consequential technology in history demands an organization structurally committed to both capability and safety. That conviction reaches every dimension of the organization: how we hire staff, the research we perform, the policy positions we adopt, and the choices we make about the deployment of our models. As a result, we are able to achieve breakthroughs that we believe would be impossible in a culture where safety, model capability, and commercial success are treated as opposing forces.
All seven of Anthropic’s co-founders remain active leaders in the organization. It is uncommon to see this level of continuity in the founding team of a technology company, including at other major frontier labs. The continuity reflects a genuinely mission-driven and high-trust team.

location: BUSINESS > Our Culture, Values, and Talent > Our Culture
text:
Our Culture
Several features of our culture are distinctive and difficult for any organization to replicate:
•We Use What We Build. We are one of the most intensive users of our own technology. Over 90% of the contributions to our codebase in September 2026 were written by Claude, and Claude is embedded in workflows across all teams at the company. When every team relies on the product daily, the feedback loop between builder and user is compressed: deficiencies can be found rapidly, and improvements are felt company-wide.
•Researching Both Safety and Capability. At the same time we advance the frontier, we develop the policies and techniques designed to keep our models safe. We were the first frontier lab to adopt a formal Responsible Scaling Policy tying safety evaluations to capability thresholds, which was co-developed by the same researchers who build our models. Our alignment and mechanistic interpretability research are examples of active scientific fields that help us understand ever-more-capable versions of Claude.
•We Optimize for Talent Density. As of September 30, 2026, with approximately 5,300 employees, our TTM revenue per employee was over $6.6 million—a reflection of extraordinary talent density and a culture built to compound it. Our employees are known internally as “Ants”—a nickname that captures the collaborative, ego-light culture of the team. Ants include many of the researchers and developers defining the frontier of AI, alongside proven operators across disciplines. Shared purpose paired with low ego translates directly into less organizational friction and greater impact per employee. Claude compounds that impact further: Ants use Claude across every function to take on work that would otherwise require substantially larger teams—allowing us to remain remarkably lean relative to our output.
•Rigor Applied to Every Function. A majority of our workforce works in research, engineering, and product development. But the culture of intellectual rigor extends to non-technical functions as well: our policy team publishes detailed policy frameworks and proposals; our go-to-market team co-develops deployment architectures alongside customers; and our Applied AI engineers sit at the frontier of what is possible with agentic systems. Our teams operate in a truth-seeking environment where the best argument wins, not the loudest voice or the most senior title. The result is a company where the distance between a research insight and a released product is unusually short.
title: US-PROSPECTUS (S-1/A, preliminary) | BUSINESS > Our Culture, Values, and Talent > Our Culture

location: BUSINESS > Our Culture, Values, and Talent > Our Values
text:
Our Values
Our values guide daily decisions across the company—from hiring and research prioritization to product development and customer engagement. We chose them because they reflect how we actually work:
•Act for the Global Good. We strive to make decisions that maximize positive outcomes for humanity over the long run and are willing to take bold action to ensure our technology is a positive force.
•Hold Light and Shade. We stay hopeful about what AI can achieve while remaining clear-eyed about what could go wrong. Both perspectives are essential, and neither can be sacrificed for the other.
•Be Good to Our Users. We define “users” broadly: customers, policymakers, our team, and anyone affected by the technology we build or the actions we take. Going above and beyond for each of them— not just meeting their immediate needs but considering downstream consequences and societal effects —is our baseline expectation, not an exception.
•Race to the Top on Safety. We believe building reliable, trustworthy, and secure AI systems is a collective responsibility and that the market will reward it. We work to set the industry bar for AI safety and inspire a dynamic where companies must compete on safety.
•Do the Simple Thing That Works. We take an empirical approach to problems and solve for the size of our impact. We try to identify the simplest solutions and iterate from there.
•Be Helpful, Honest, and Harmless. These principles guide Claude’s behavior and reflect how we operate as an organization: a high-trust, low-ego team that communicates kindly and directly, assumes good intentions even in disagreement, and pitches in where needed, regardless of role or team.
•Put the Mission First. Our mission is the arbiter when tradeoffs arise between speed and safety, short-term revenue and long-term trust, competitive pressure and responsible development. Our mission gives us shared purpose, engenders trust and collaboration, and ensures that no one is a bystander in our success.

text:
Our Talent
As of September 30, 2026, we had approximately 5,300 employees worldwide, a majority of whom work in research, engineering, and product development functions. Our team includes researchers who originated several foundational advances in AI, including RLHF, Constitutional AI, GPT-2 and GPT-3, and mechanistic interpretability, who developed the first Responsible Scaling Policy to be formally adopted by a frontier lab tying safety evaluations to model capability thresholds, and who authored the foundational paper on Scaling Laws. Our team draws from a range of disciplines and includes award-winning computer scientists, physicists, neuroscientists, mathematicians, and policy researchers, as well as seasoned engineering and go-to-market leaders, united by the conviction that the most consequential technology in history requires the most talented team building it. We believe our culture and mission alignment enable us to hire and retain the talent required to continuously push the frontier of AI forward in a safe and responsible way.
We design our human capital programs to attract, retain, and reward top talent through equity incentive plans and other compensation, while supporting employees’ continual growth and reinforcing our culture and values. In certain countries in which we operate, we are subject to, and comply with, local labor law requirements that may automatically make our employees subject to industry-wide collective bargaining agreements.
We believe that building AI systems that serve all of humanity requires a team that reflects the range of communities we serve. The interdisciplinary nature of our work means we actively seek talent from non-traditional backgrounds for an AI company, such as philosophy, journalism, and education, and we believe this breadth of perspective directly strengthens both the safety and capability of our research. We are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where employees of all backgrounds can contribute, grow, and thrive.

location: BUSINESS > Research Lab Identity and the Research-to-Product Pipeline
text: We are first and foremost a research lab. We develop the foundational science to train frontier models, perform rigorous research to understand these models’ inner workings, and develop techniques to align these models to human values and make them safe.
title: US-PROSPECTUS (S-1/A, preliminary) | BUSINESS > Research Lab Identity and the Research-to-Product Pipeline

location: BUSINESS > Research Lab Identity and the Research-to-Product Pipeline > Research Philosophy
text:
Research Philosophy
Our research culture is organized around a principle we apply across the company: do the simple thing that works. We pursue continuous, empirically validated improvements to data composition, model architecture, and training methodology, all of which must demonstrate measurable gains that hold as models increase in scale. This is why we currently focus on software development and agentic capabilities: these are areas where economic impact is large; where safety concerns manifest, making them a test bed for safety research; and where outputs are largely verifiable.
Every research project must ultimately advance our mission. This focus also guides what we choose not to pursue. For example, we do not currently focus on developing video and image generation models, despite their commercial appeal. That compute instead goes to coding, agentic skills, and safety research—a research decision that has also aided the capital efficiency of our models.
Our research culture is highly collaborative and transparent. When multiple teams pursue parallel approaches, the norm is to consolidate behind the approach with the best empirical results rather than the loudest voice or most senior person in the room. This requires institutional trust we have built since our earliest days, and we believe it is a primary reason our research velocity has scaled significantly faster than headcount.
title: US-PROSPECTUS (S-1/A, preliminary) | BUSINESS > Research Lab Identity and the Research-to-Product Pipeline > Research Philosophy

location: BUSINESS > Research Lab Identity and the Research-to-Product Pipeline > How Research Becomes Product
text:
How Research Becomes Product
Anthropic was founded on the empirical conviction that Scaling Laws are the primary engine of AI progress. We operate with a sustained rigor in how we allocate research resources, including talent and compute, and measure whether each investment translates into scaled model performance. We believe that sustained and focused research can allow us to advance at an accelerated rate beyond what Scaling Laws alone predict through our compute multiplier advancements that have allowed us to push the frontier of model capability with better compute efficiency.
Pre-training. Our pre-training process operates as a disciplined pipeline. Researchers propose potential improvements to model architecture, training methodology, or data composition, and each candidate is then validated at a smaller scale before we permit it to consume large amounts of compute. We set a high bar for inclusion in a frontier training run; we require evidence that demonstrates a given improvement holds as models increase in size. Frontier training runs are themselves planned capital deployments with defined inputs and strict inclusion criteria. Although not every run performs as our researchers expect, the process is designed to turn research investment into predictable capability gains with greater consistency over time.
Post-training. Pre-training produces raw model capability. During post-training, that capability is refined into practical utility—the ability to write production-quality code, operate software tools, follow complex multi-step instructions, and act autonomously on a user’s behalf. This phase has evolved from a minor adjustment step into one of the largest areas of our research investment, reflecting the evolution in model capability from conversational assistants to autonomous agents that perform tasks independently. Post-training centers on training models against complete, realistic tasks whose complexity reflects the demands of real professional environments. We have made substantial proprietary investments in developing this task portfolio, and its breadth and realism constitute one of our most durable scientific advantages, which we believe is difficult to observe from outside the organization and correspondingly difficult to replicate.
Inference. Our model architecture and inference infrastructure are co-designed. AI researchers and inference infrastructure engineers share planning cycles, reporting lines, and performance targets. Model architecture decisions are made with inference economics as a priority, which is why successive versions of Claude models can deliver both higher capability and greater efficiency than their predecessors.

text: Any technology that is powerful enough to produce the enormous benefits that we believe AI will bring also poses risks. Responding to these risks requires a portfolio of safety research that spans how we train, evaluate, interpret, secure, and monitor our models.
