The Trust Amendment Threshold may be satisfied as follows: •if the Trustees are voting in favor of the action, upon approval of 80% of the authorized members of our board of directors and 80% of the Trustees then in office (in each case, rounded up or down to the nearest whole number (any exact 0.5 rounding up)); •if our Class F common stock remains outstanding and the Trustees are not voting in favor of the action: ◦until the third anniversary of the completion of this offering, upon approval by (i) our Class F common stock acting pursuant to the unanimous approval of the Continuing Founders, (ii) a majority of the votes cast by our Class E common stock (subject to a quorum of 40% of our outstanding Class E common stock), and (iii) a majority of the votes cast by outstanding Class A common stock (subject to a quorum of a majority of outstanding Class A common stock); or ◦at any time, upon approval by (i) our Class F common stock acting by decision of 66 2/3% of the Continuing Founders (rounded up to the nearest whole number), (ii) 75% of the votes cast by our Class E common stock (subject to a quorum of a majority of outstanding Class E common stock), and (iii) a majority of the votes cast by our Class A common stock (subject to a quorum of a majority of outstanding Class A common stock); or | The Class F Sunset Time occurs on the earlier of (i) the time when no Class F common stock remains outstanding, including due to the redemption of our Class F common stock agreed to by a Supermajority of the Continuing Founders or upon the dissolution of the Founder LLC, and (ii) the completion of the Class F Transition Period. The Class F Transition Period commences when there have been fewer than three Continuing Founders (not including any successor member who is a “Non-Qualifying Member” as defined in the Founder LLC Agreement) for 90 consecutive calendar days. A Continuing Founder will be removed from the Founder LLC upon the earliest to occur of (i) such Continuing Founder’s resignation as a member of the Founder LLC; (ii) such Continuing Founder’s death or incapacity; (iii) with respect to each of our seven original co-founders, such original co-founder’s ceasing to hold (together with such original co-founder’s related holders) on any record date for a vote of our stockholders a number of shares of Class A common stock (including shares subject to options, RSUs, and other convertible securities) equal to at least 2% of the shares of Class A common stock held by such original co-founder and their related holders as of the completion of this offering; (iv) such Continuing Founder’s removal for “cause,” which includes specified competitive activities described in the Founder LLC Agreement; (v) with respect to any successor member admitted to the Founder LLC prior to the commencement of the Class F Transition Period, other than a successor member who is a member during the Class F Transition Period, the tenth anniversary of the completion of this offering; or (vi) with respect to each of our seven original co- founders, the commencement of a leave of absence approved by a Supermajority of the other Continuing Founders, which may not be approved during the Class F Transition Period or if the grant of the leave of absence would itself cause the Class F Transition Period to commence.

After the completion of this offering and the closing of the concurrent private placement, the holders of up to 8,527,685,412 shares of our Class A common stock (including those issuable upon conversion of our Class N common stock) will be entitled to certain demand registration rights, including those set forth in our IRA and Google’s registration rights described below under “—Registration Rights of Google.” Under our IRA, at any time beginning six months after the effective date of this offering, the holders of at least 60% of the shares registrable under our IRA that are entitled to vote can request that we register the offer and sale of their shares. If we determine that it would be seriously detrimental to us and our stockholders to effect such a demand registration, we have the right to defer such registration, not more than twice in any 12-month period, for a period of up to 120 days. location: DESCRIPTION OF CAPITAL STOCK > Anti-Takeover Provisions > Delaware Law
text:
Delaware Law
We have elected not to be governed by the provisions of Section 203 of the DGCL prior to the later to occur of the Class F Sunset Time and the Class T Sunset Time, but our amended and restated certificate of incorporation will provide that the restrictions contained in Section 203 will apply to us immediately following the later to occur of either the Class F Sunset Time or the Class T Sunset Time. Following the later to occur of the Class F Sunset Time or the Class T Sunset Time, we will thereafter be governed by Section 203, which generally prohibits a public Delaware corporation from engaging in a “business combination” with an “interested stockholder” for a period of three years after the date of the transaction in which the person became an interested stockholder, unless:
•the business combination or transaction which resulted in the stockholder becoming an interested stockholder was approved by the board of directors prior to the time that the stockholder became an interested stockholder;
•upon consummation of the transaction which resulted in the stockholder becoming an interested stockholder, the interested stockholder owned at least 85% in voting power of the voting stock of the corporation outstanding at the time the transaction commenced, excluding shares owned by directors who are also officers of the corporation and shares owned by employee stock plans in which employee participants do not have the right to determine confidentially whether shares held subject to the plan will be tendered in a tender or exchange offer; or
•at or subsequent to the time the stockholder became an interested stockholder, the business combination was approved by the board of directors and authorized at an annual or special meeting of the stockholders, and not by written consent, by the affirmative vote of at least two-thirds of the outstanding voting stock which is not owned by the interested stockholder.
In general, Section 203 defines a “business combination” to include mergers, asset sales, and other transactions resulting in financial benefit to a stockholder and an “interested stockholder” as a person who, together with affiliates and associates, owns, or is an affiliate or associate of the corporation and within three years did own, 15% or more in voting power of the corporation’s outstanding voting stock.

text:
Amended and Restated Certificate of Incorporation and Amended and Restated Bylaws Provisions
Our amended and restated certificate of incorporation and our amended and restated bylaws, which will become effective immediately prior to the completion of this offering, will include a number of provisions that could deter hostile takeovers or delay or prevent changes in control of our board of directors or management team, including but not limited to the following:
Multi-Class Common Stock
As described above in the section titled “—Common Stock—Voting Rights,” our amended and restated certificate of incorporation provides for a multi-class common stock structure. Under this governance structure, we expect that the LTBT and the Founder LLC will collectively have the ability to elect all members of our board of directors, and the Founder LLC will have the ability to determine the outcome of all matters submitted to a vote of our stockholders generally for the foreseeable future, including the approval by our stockholders of significant corporate transactions such as a merger or other sale of our company or its assets. Such transactions also require approval of our board of directors, a majority of whom are elected by the LTBT. Holders of our Class A common stock generally will not be able to affect the outcome of any matter submitted to a vote of our stockholders or the election of our directors, regardless of how they vote, unless a majority of the Continuing Founders cannot agree on how our Class F common stock will be voted (in which case our Class F common stock will generally be voted proportionately with the votes of our Class A common stock cast on the matter).
Classified Board
Our amended and restated certificate of incorporation that will become effective immediately prior to the completion of this offering will provide that prior to the Class F Sunset Time, we will not have a classified board of directors, and all directors will be elected for annual terms. Each director’s term will continue until the next annual meeting and until the election and qualification of their successor, or their earlier death, resignation, or removal.

location: DESCRIPTION OF CAPITAL STOCK > Anti-Takeover Provisions > Amended and Restated Certificate of Incorporation and Amended and Restated Bylaws Provisions
text:
Following the Class F Sunset Time, our board of directors will shift to having a classified board of directors consisting of three classes of approximately equal size, each serving staggered three-year terms. At such time, our directors would be assigned by the then-current board of directors to a class. If our Class T common stock remains outstanding, the Class T directors and the remaining directors shall be allocated among the classes so that each class includes a proportionate number of Class T directors and other directors. Upon expiration of the term of a class of directors, directors for that class would each be elected for a three-year term at the annual meeting of stockholders in the year in which that term expires. As a result, only one class of directors would be elected at each annual meeting of our stockholders, with the other classes continuing for the remainder of their respective three-year terms. Each director’s term would continue until the third annual meeting of stockholders following their election and until their successor has been elected and qualified, or until their earlier death, resignation, or removal. Any increase or decrease in the number of directors would be distributed among the three classes so that, as nearly as practicable, each class would consist of one-third of our directors.

text:
Our amended and restated certificate of incorporation and amended and restated bylaws will provide that (i) prior to the Class T Sunset Time, only the holder of our Class T common stock can fill vacant directorships of any Class T director, subject to the nomination procedures for the Specified Class T Director; and (ii) prior to the Class F Sunset Time, vacant or newly created directorships for any directors other than our Class T directors can be filled by (A) our board of directors, in accordance with, and following receipt of written notice from, the Founder LLC recommending the person proposed to fill such director seat or (B) the holders of our Class A common stock and Class F common stock, voting together or acting by written consent. Following the Class F Sunset Time, only our board of directors will be permitted to fill vacant or newly created directorships for any directors other than our Class T directors. Prior to the Class T Sunset Time, the number of directors constituting our board of directors will be permitted to be set only with the approval of 80% of the authorized members of our board of directors (rounded up or down to the nearest whole number (any exact 0.5 rounding up)); provided that until the earlier to occur of the Class F Sunset Time or the Class T Sunset Time, such total number of authorized directors must be an odd number. Following the Class T Sunset Time, the number of directors constituting our board of directors will be permitted to be set with the approval of a majority of the authorized members of our board of directors. These provisions would prevent a stockholder from increasing the size of our board of directors and then gaining control of our board of directors by filling the resulting vacancies with its own nominees. This will make it more difficult to change the composition of our board of directors.

text:
Our amended and restated bylaws will provide advance notice procedures for stockholders, other than holders of Class T common stock or Class F common stock nominating directors in accordance with nomination procedures in our certificate of incorporation or the Stockholders’ Agreement, seeking to bring business before our annual meeting of stockholders or to nominate candidates for election as directors at a meeting of stockholders. Our amended and restated bylaws will also specify certain requirements regarding the form and content of a stockholder’s notice. These provisions might preclude our stockholders from bringing matters before our annual meeting of stockholders or from making nominations for directors at a meeting of stockholders if the proper procedures are not followed. In addition, our NGC will have the right to receive 30 days’ prior written notice of any nomination of persons to serve as a director by the LTBT or the Founder LLC or the proposed removal of such directors, as well as appointments and removals of the Trustees. Our NGC may waive such notice periods in its discretion. We expect that these provisions may also discourage or deter a potential acquirer from conducting a solicitation of proxies to elect the acquirer’s own slate of directors or otherwise attempting to obtain control of our company.
Special Meetings of Stockholders
Our amended and restated certificate of incorporation and amended and restated bylaws will provide that special meetings of stockholders may be called only by (i) our board of directors acting pursuant to a resolution adopted by a majority of the authorized members of our board of directors; (ii) the chairperson of our board of directors; (iii) our Chief Executive Officer; (iv) our President; (v) following the Class F Sunset Time, a majority of the directors who are not Class T directors; (vi) prior to the Class F Sunset Time and only with respect to a special meeting at which holders of our Class E common stock will be asked to vote on a proposal, the secretary of the company; or (vii) prior to the Class F Sunset Time, the Founder LLC as the holder of our Class F common stock.
No Cumulative Voting
The DGCL provides that stockholders are not entitled to cumulate votes in the election of directors unless a corporation’s certificate of incorporation provides otherwise. Our amended and restated certificate of incorporation does not provide for cumulative voting.
Action by Written Consent

text:
Prior to the Class F Sunset Time and the Class T Sunset Time, stockholders may act by written consent only with respect to (i) any action to nominate, elect, or remove directors or appoint a director to fill any vacancy or newly created directorship; (ii) any action to satisfy certain redemption and protective provisions in our amended and restated certificate of incorporation related to our Class F common stock, Class T common stock, and Class E common stock; and (iii) any matter on which stockholders vote together as a single class if such matter is first approved or requested by our board of directors. From and after the Class T Sunset Time, only the holder of the share of Class F common stock may act by written consent, and from and after the Class F Sunset Time, only the holder of the share of Class T common stock may act by written consent, in each case, only with respect to the actions described above. From and after the occurrence of both the Class F Sunset Time and the Class T Sunset Time, any action required or permitted to be taken by the stockholders must be effected at a duly called annual or special meeting of stockholders and may not be effected by any consent in writing by such stockholders. Notwithstanding the foregoing, any action required or permitted to be taken by the holders of Class E common stock must be effected at a duly called annual or special meeting of stockholders and may not be effected by any consent in writing by such stockholders.
Amendment of Certificate of Incorporation and Bylaws Provisions
Prior to the Class F Sunset Time, a majority of the voting power of our Class A common stock and Class F common stock, voting together as a single class, can amend certain provisions in our amended and restated certificate of incorporation and our amended and restated bylaws. Following the Class F Sunset Time, 66 2/3% of the voting power of our Class A common stock can amend certain provisions in our amended and restated certificate of incorporation and our amended and restated bylaws.

text: Section 22 of the Securities Act establishes concurrent jurisdiction for federal and state courts over Securities Act claims. Accordingly, both state and federal courts have jurisdiction to hear such claims. To prevent having to litigate claims in multiple jurisdictions and the threat of inconsistent or contrary rulings by different courts, among other considerations, our amended and restated bylaws will also provide that, unless we consent in writing to the selection of an alternative forum, the federal district courts of the United States will, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, be the sole and exclusive forum for resolving any complaint asserting a cause or causes of action arising under the Securities Act against any person in connection with any offering of our securities, including, without limitation, any auditor, underwriter, expert, control person, or other defendant. Unless we consent in writing to the selection of an alternative forum, the United States District Court for the District of Delaware will, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, be the sole and exclusive forum for the resolution of any derivative action or proceeding brought to enforce any duty or liability created by the Exchange Act or the rules or regulations thereunder. All other claims arising under the Exchange Act may be brought in any federal court of competent jurisdiction. Any person or entity purchasing, holding, or otherwise acquiring any interest in our securities shall be deemed to have notice of and consented to these provisions. We note that stockholders cannot waive compliance (or consent to non-compliance) with the federal securities laws and the rules and regulations thereunder.

location: DESCRIPTION OF CAPITAL STOCK > Founder LLC Agreement
text:
Our co-founders intend to enter into the Founder LLC Agreement. We expect the Founder LLC Agreement to become effective substantially concurrently with the filing and acceptance of our amended and restated certificate of incorporation with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware.
Our Class F common stock will be held by the Founder LLC. Our Class F common stock will be voted by the Founder LLC in a manner determined pursuant to the Founder LLC Agreement. Generally, the Founder LLC will vote as determined by a majority of the Continuing Founders. Our seven co-founders will each initially be a Continuing Founder. Upon the incapacity or death of any of our co-founders, a successor member may be admitted to the Founder LLC as a Continuing Founder until the tenth anniversary of the completion of this offering.
When there have been fewer than three Continuing Founders (not including any successor member who is a “Non-Qualifying Member” as defined in the Founder LLC Agreement) for 90 consecutive calendar days, the 450-day Class F Transition Period will commence. Upon completion of the Class F Transition Period, all of our Class F common stock and Class E common stock then issued and outstanding will be redeemed by us for no consideration and certain other governance changes will take effect.
Regardless of the length of time that has elapsed since the completion of this offering or the circumstances that resulted in the removal of a Continuing Founder, one or more successor members may be admitted to the Founder LLC during the Class F Transition Period as needed to ensure that there are three Continuing Founders serving until completion of the Class F Transition Period. The admission of any successor member during the Class F Transition Period will not cure the event that commenced the Class F Transition Period or extend the Class F Transition Period.
title: US-PROSPECTUS (S-1/A, preliminary) | DESCRIPTION OF CAPITAL STOCK > Founder LLC Agreement

location: DESCRIPTION OF CAPITAL STOCK > Founder LLC Agreement
text:
A Continuing Founder will be removed from the Founder LLC upon the earliest to occur of (i) such Continuing Founder’s resignation as a member of the Founder LLC; (ii) such Continuing Founder’s death or incapacity; (iii) with respect to each of our seven original co-founders, such original co-founder’s ceasing to hold (together with such original co-founder’s related holders) on any record date for a vote of our stockholders a number of shares of Class A common stock (including shares subject to options, RSUs, and other convertible securities) equal to at least 2% of the shares of Class A common stock held by such original co-founder and their related holders as of the completion of this offering; (iv) such Continuing Founder’s removal for “cause” (as defined in the Founder LLC Agreement), which includes specified competitive activities described in the Founder LLC Agreement; (v) with respect to any successor member admitted to the Founder LLC prior to the commencement of the Class F Transition Period, other than a successor member who is a member during the Class F Transition Period, the tenth anniversary of the completion of this offering; or (vi) with respect to each of our seven original co-founders, the commencement of a leave of absence approved by a Supermajority of the other Continuing Founders, which may not be approved during the Class F Transition Period or if the grant of the leave of absence would itself cause the Class F Transition Period to commence.
Each Continuing Founder will be entitled to one vote when determining how our Class F common stock will be voted. If a majority of the Continuing Founders cannot agree on how our Class F common stock will be voted, then our Class F common stock will generally be voted proportionately with the votes of our Class A common stock cast on the matter (subject to a quorum of a majority of outstanding Class A common stock). With respect to certain matters, our Class F common stock will be voted “for” the proposal only if a greater threshold of Continuing Founders agree, and if the greater threshold is not met, our Class F common stock will be voted “against” the proposal. See the section titled “—Class F Common Stock Voting Mechanics.”

location: DESCRIPTION OF CAPITAL STOCK > Class F Common Stock Voting Mechanics
text: ______________ (1)Each Continuing Founder will be entitled to one vote when determining how our Class F common stock will be voted. (2)If a majority of the Continuing Founders deliver the same instruction as to how the votes corresponding to our Class F common stock shall be cast, including “for,” “against,” or “withhold,” but excluding an instruction to “abstain,” our Class F common stock will be voted accordingly. If a majority of the Continuing Founders deliver instructions to “abstain” or do not deliver the same or any instructions, our Class F common stock will be voted proportionately with the votes of Class A common stock cast (subject to a quorum of a majority of outstanding Class A common stock). (3)“Supermajority” means the total number of Continuing Founders entitled to vote, minus one, delivers instructions to vote “for” the proposal. If there are fewer than three Continuing Founders, a Supermajority requires unanimity of Continuing Founders. (4)If a proposal requires both a Supermajority and a Trust Amendment Supermajority, both thresholds must be satisfied. (5)A “Trust Amendment Supermajority” will be satisfied if (i) 66 2/3% of the Continuing Founders, rounded up to the nearest whole number, deliver instructions to vote “for” the proposal, and approval by 75% of the votes cast by our Class E common stock (subject to a quorum of a majority of outstanding Class E common stock) and a majority of the votes cast by our Class A common stock (subject to a quorum of a majority of the outstanding shares of Class A common stock) is also obtained or (ii) until the third anniversary of the completion of this offering, the Continuing Founders unanimously deliver instructions to vote “for” the proposal, and approval by a majority of the votes cast by our Class E common stock (subject to a quorum of 40% of our outstanding Class E common stock) and a majority of the votes cast by our outstanding Class A common stock (subject to a quorum of a majority of outstanding shares of Class A common stock) is also obtained.

location: SHARES ELIGIBLE FOR FUTURE SALE > Rule 144
text:
In general, Rule 144 provides that once we have been subject to the public company reporting requirements of Section 13 or Section 15(d) of the Exchange Act for at least 90 days, a person who is not deemed to have been one of our affiliates for purposes of the Securities Act at any time during the 90 days preceding a sale and who has beneficially owned the shares of our Class A common stock proposed to be sold for at least six months is entitled to sell those shares without complying with the manner of sale, volume limitation, or notice provisions of Rule 144, subject to compliance with the public information requirements of Rule 144. If such a person has beneficially owned the shares proposed to be sold for at least one year, including the holding period of any prior owner other than our affiliates, then that person would be entitled to sell those shares without complying with any of the requirements of Rule 144.
In general, Rule 144 provides that our affiliates or persons selling shares of our Class A common stock on behalf of our affiliates are entitled to sell upon expiration of the lock-up and market standoff agreements described above, within any three-month period, a number of shares of our Class A common stock that does not exceed the greater of:
•1% of the number of shares of our Class A common stock then outstanding, which will equal 74,279,918 shares immediately after the completion of this offering; or
•the average weekly trading volume of our Class A common stock during the four calendar weeks preceding the filing of a notice on Form 144 with respect to that sale.
Sales of our Class A common stock made in reliance upon Rule 144 by our affiliates or persons selling shares of our Class A common stock on behalf of our affiliates are also subject to certain manner of sale provisions and notice requirements and to the availability of current public information about us.
title: US-PROSPECTUS (S-1/A, preliminary) | SHARES ELIGIBLE FOR FUTURE SALE > Rule 144

location: SHARES ELIGIBLE FOR FUTURE SALE > Rule 701
text: Rule 701 generally allows a stockholder who purchased shares of our capital stock pursuant to a written compensatory plan or contract and who is not deemed to have been an affiliate of our company during the immediately preceding 90 days to sell these shares in reliance upon Rule 144, but without being required to comply with the public information, holding period, volume limitation, or notice provisions of Rule 144. Rule 701 also permits affiliates of our company to sell their Rule 701 shares under Rule 144 without complying with the holding period requirements of Rule 144. All holders of Rule 701 shares, however, are required to wait until 90 days after the date of this prospectus before selling those shares pursuant to Rule 701.

text:
In order to facilitate the offering of our Class A common stock, Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC, acting as stabilization agent on behalf of the underwriters, may engage in transactions that stabilize, maintain, or otherwise affect the price of our Class A common stock. Specifically, the underwriter may sell more shares of Class A common stock than the underwriters are obligated to purchase under the underwriting agreement, creating a short position. A short sale is covered if the short position is no greater than the number of shares available for purchase under the underwriter’s option to purchase additional shares. The underwriter can close out a covered short sale by exercising the underwriter’s option to purchase additional shares or purchasing shares in the open market. In determining the source of shares to close out a covered short sale, the underwriter will consider, among other things, the open market price of our Class A common stock compared to the price available under the underwriter’s option to purchase additional shares. The underwriter may also sell shares of Class A common stock in excess of the underwriter’s option to purchase additional shares, creating a naked short position. The underwriter must close out any naked short position by purchasing shares of Class A common stock in the open market. A naked short position is more likely to be created if the underwriter is concerned that there may be downward pressure on the price of our Class A common stock in the open market after pricing that could adversely affect investors who purchase shares of Class A common stock in this offering. As an additional means of facilitating this offering, the underwriter may bid for, and purchase, shares of Class A common stock in the open market to stabilize the price of our Class A common stock. These activities may raise or maintain the market price of our Class A common stock above independent market levels or prevent or slow a decline in the market price of our Class A common stock. The underwriter is not required to engage in these activities and may end any of these activities at any time.
The underwriters may offer and sell the shares of common stock through certain of their affiliates or other registered broker-dealers or selling agents.

text: We have a novel capital and corporate governance structure. We are incorporated as a public benefit corporation under Delaware law, a structure consistent with our commitment to artificial intelligence (“AI”) safety and responsibility. As a public benefit corporation, we are required to balance the pecuniary interests of our stockholders, the best interests of those materially affected by our conduct, and the specific public benefit purpose identified in our amended and restated certificate of incorporation: the responsible development and maintenance of advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity. We created our Long-Term Benefit Trust (the “LTBT”) to help ensure that Anthropic, PBC is managed in a manner that responsibly balances its goals as a public benefit corporation. The LTBT is intended to operate as an independent body of five financially disinterested trustees with expertise in AI safety, national security, public policy, and social enterprise. Through a special class of common stock, Class T common stock, the LTBT generally has the authority to elect and remove the Class T directors, who together will constitute a majority of the authorized members of our board of directors. Our Class T common stock does not otherwise have voting rights with respect to matters submitted to stockholders generally and has no economic rights. Immediately prior to the completion of the global offering, we will also issue a single share of Class F common stock, a special class of our common stock (the “Class F Stock Issuance”), to a limited liability company organized by our co-founders (the “Founder LLC”). [Co-founder 1 (CEO)], our Chief Executive Officer and a member of our board of directors, and [Co-founder 2 (President)], our President and Chairperson of our board of directors, together with our five other co-founders, will initially be the sole members of the Founder LLC. Our Class F common stock, which will be held by the Founder LLC, will be entitled to an aggregate number of votes that equals 50.1% of the total voting power of our outstanding shares of capital stock with respect to matters submitted to stockholders generally, including the election of our directors other than the Class T directors. Immediately prior to the global offering, we will also authorize a special class of our common stock, Class E common stock, which we will issue to our employees, excluding our co-founders.

Our Class E common stock will be entitled to vote only on certain limited matters and will not have any economic rights.
Principal Activities – Anthropic was founded in 2021 by a team of researchers responsible for many of the breakthroughs that define super intelligence. We are first and foremost a research lab—our mission is the responsible development and maintenance of advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity. This mission directs our focus—along with our talent and culture, our frontier and safety research, our approach to compute (i.e., the computational processing resources used to train and run super intelligence models, including, without limitation, specialized accelerators, memory, networking, storage, and power systems that are deployed in data centers or other physical computing environments), and our enterprise strategy, it is one of the core advantages that set us apart. These advantages enable us to continuously advance frontier intelligence and shape the standards for its safe and responsible development. Our frontier intelligence (referring to super intelligence systems at the current leading edge of capability and safety, performing at or near the highest levels of any existing system across a broad range of tasks), Claude, is delivered to customers through our models, platform, and applications. In our assessment, Claude has experienced the fastest enterprise adoption of any technology in history, as demonstrated by revenue growing from $0 at commercial launch in the first quarter of 2023 to $17.0 billion for the three months ended September 30, 2026 (unaudited). This rapid and growing adoption generates two self-reinforcing dynamics—an improvement loop that advances Claude and an investment loop that helps fund our continued research at the frontier.

B.3 What are the key risks that are specific to the issuer?
An investment in our shares of Class A common stock is subject to a number of risks. The following risks are key risks specific to us: • Our models have in the past behaved, and may in the future behave, in unintended, misaligned, or autonomous ways, including by taking harmful actions that no user or third party directed, which could adversely affect our reputation and brand, business, financial condition, and results of operations.
• Our success depends in large part on our ability to continue to develop the most advanced and capable AI models, and any failure to do so could adversely affect our business.
• If we are unable to secure adequate compute or if we fail to direct our compute effectively across our workloads, we may be unable to train models that remain competitive with those of our competitors or adequately serve our customers.
• Constraints on the critical inputs supporting compute could limit our ability to secure adequate compute.
• We are highly dependent on the continued service of our co-founders, senior management team, and key technical employees, and the loss of any of these individuals may adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. • Our company culture has contributed to our success and, if we cannot maintain this culture as we grow, our business could be adversely affected.
• We face intense competition, and if we are unable to compete effectively, our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected.
• If the market for our models, platform, and applications develops more slowly than we expect or declines, our growth may slow or stall, and our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected.
• If the use of our AI models results in harm, whether through use by malicious actors or misuse by other third parties, or if our model guardrails or safeguards fail to prevent such misuse, our reputation and brand, business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected.
• We may be exposed to liability, litigation, and regulatory action arising from harms associated with our AI models, and our contractual protections and insurance may be insufficient, any of which could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.

C.1 What are the main features of the securities?
a) General information on our capital stock Upon the completion of the global offering, we will have five classes of authorized capital stock: a class designated as participating common stock, a class designated as Class T common stock (the “Class T common stock”), a class designated as Class F common stock (the “Class F common stock”), a class designated as Class E common stock (the “Class E common stock”), and a class designated as preferred stock. The class of capital stock designated as participating common stock will be divided into two series, designated Class A common stock (the “Class A common stock”) and Class N common stock (the “Class N common stock”). The rights of the holders of Class A common stock and Class N common stock will be identical, except with respect to voting and conversion, with each share of Class A common stock being entitled to one vote per share, overall limited to 49.9% with respect to matters submitted to stockholders generally by the voting rights attached to our Class F common stock as described below, and shares of Class N common stock having no voting rights, except as otherwise required by law, and being convertible into Class A common stock upon a sale or transfer to an unaffiliated third party. Our Class T common stock is, and will continue to be, a special class of stock that is issued to the LTBT. Through our Class T common stock, the LTBT generally has the authority to elect and remove the Class T directors, who together will constitute a majority of the authorized members of our board of directors. The share of our Class T common stock does not otherwise have voting rights with respect to matters submitted to stockholders generally and has no economic rights. Our Class F common stock is a special class of our common stock, consisting of a single share, that will be issued to the Founder LLC, and will be entitled to an aggregate number of votes that equals 50.1% of the total voting power of our outstanding shares of capital stock as of the applicable record date with respect to matters submitted to stockholders generally, including the election of our directors other than the Class T directors. Our Class F common stock will not have any economic rights.

Scope of European Retail Offering – The European retail shares are offered to retail investors in Germany, Denmark, Finland, France, Ireland, the Netherlands, Norway, Spain and Sweden.
Simultaneous Swiss Retail Offering – The European retail shares are at the same time offered to retail investors in Switzerland on the basis of this prospectus as filed with a Swiss prospectus office for automatic acceptance in accordance with Article 54(2) of the Swiss Financial Services Act (“FinSA”) (the “Swiss retail offering”). The simultaneous public offering of the European retail shares in the Swiss retail offering is solely made by the Company together with UBS AG, Bahnhofstrasse 45, 8001 Zurich, Switzerland (the “Swiss underwriter”) and is made on the terms applicable to the European retail offering.
Eligibility Criteria for Investors – The European retail offering is solely addressed to individual persons or legal entities which do not qualify as qualified investors within the meaning of Article 2 point (e) of the Prospectus Regulation (referred to as retail investors) and which are resident or located in any of the Covered EEA Countries. The Prospectus Regulation defines qualified investors as persons or entities that are listed in points (1) to (4) of Section I of Annex II to Directive 2014/65/EU, as amended (“MiFID II”), and persons or entities who are, on request, treated as professional clients in accordance with Section II of that Annex, or recognized as eligible counterparties in accordance with Article 30 of MiFID II unless they have entered into an agreement with their bank or financial intermediary to be treated as non-professional clients in accordance with the fourth paragraph of Section I of that Annex.
The Swiss retail offering is solely addressed to individual persons or legal entities which do not qualify as professional clients within the meaning of the FinSA. The FinSA defines “professional clients” as those persons or entities that either (i) are listed in Article 4(3) FinSA and which have not declared an opting-in pursuant to Article 5(5) FinSA or (ii) have requested to be treated as professional clients (opting-out) pursuant to Article 5(1) FinSA.

text: Net Proceeds and Use of Proceeds – We estimate that the net proceeds to us from the sale of shares of our Class A common stock in the global offering and the sale of shares of our Class N common stock by us in the concurrent private placement will be approximately $84.6 billion, thereof $58.6 billion attributable to the global offering of shares of our Class A common stock (of which $5.9 billion are attributable to the European retail shares if all European retail shares are sold) and $26.0 billion attributable to the concurrent private placement of the shares of our Class N common stock, based upon the assumed initial public offering price of $74.00 per share, which is the midpoint of the estimated offering price range set for the U.S. offering, and after deducting estimated underwriting discounts and commissions (which apply only to the shares of Class A common stock sold in the global offering) and estimated offering expenses payable by us, or approximately $93.7 billion if the underwriters’ option to purchase additional shares of our Class A common stock from us is exercised in full. We will not receive any proceeds from the sale of shares of Class A common stock by the selling stockholders in the global offering. We intend to use the net proceeds from the global offering and the concurrent private placement for general corporate purposes, including working capital, operating expenses, and capital expenditures, including investments in compute and infrastructure, as well as hiring and retention of highly skilled personnel. Additionally, we may use a portion of the net proceeds we receive from the global offering to acquire or invest in businesses, products, services, or technologies. However, we do not have agreements or commitments for any material acquisitions or investments at this time. We also intend to use a portion of the net proceeds to satisfy our anticipated tax withholding and remittance obligations related to the RSU Settlement. We cannot further specify with certainty the particular uses of the net proceeds that we will receive from the global offering, and there is no order of priority for the aforementioned uses. Accordingly, we will have broad discretion in using these proceeds. Pending the use of proceeds from the global offering as described above, we may invest the net proceeds that we receive in the global offering in short- term, investment grade, interest-bearing instruments.

2.2.2 Management’s Estimates
Certain estimates in this prospectus regarding global knowledge workers’ wages, which we refer to as the annual economic value represented by global knowledge workers, are our own, derived from third-party data. Based on wage data for U.S. workers by occupation classification from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics in 2025, we calculate the total salary for the subset of workers that we believe to represent knowledge workers. Based on International Labor Organization data for global labor income as a percentage of global GDP, and based on 2025 global GDP, we estimate a 2025 global wages figure. We calculate the ratio of total U.S. wages in 2025 to the 2025 global wages figure, and apply that ratio to the total U.S. knowledge workers’ wages figure to arrive at an estimate of global knowledge workers’ wages. In addition, unless otherwise specified, the information contained in this prospectus on customer behavior, market environment, market developments, growth rates, market trends and competition in the market in which we operate is based on the Company’s assessments. These assessments, in turn, are based on our relationships with our customers, review and interpretation of publicly available financial reporting of peers, industry publications, benchmark data for our and competing AI models, our internal research and our knowledge of the market in which we currently, and will in the future, operate, as well as the sources referred to above.
This information involves several assumptions and limitations, and investors are cautioned not to give undue weight to such information. Forecasts and other forward-looking information obtained from the sources named above are subject to the same qualifications and uncertainties as the other forward-looking statements in this prospectus.

text:
The Company is incorporated under the laws of the State of Delaware, United States. None of the directors, officers or other executives of the Company are residents or citizens of the EEA. Investors may be unable to effect service of process within the EEA. Furthermore, since the Company’s assets are primarily located in the United States, any judgment obtained in the EEA against the Company may not be collectible in the EEA.
Conversely, civil liabilities based on U.S. federal or state securities laws may not be enforceable in the Covered EEA Countries and Switzerland:
Germany and Sweden: There is doubt as to the enforceability in Germany of civil liabilities based on U.S. federal or state securities laws, either in an original action or in an action to enforce a judgment obtained in U.S. federal or state courts. The United States and Germany currently do not have a treaty providing for the reciprocal recognition and enforcement of judgments, other than arbitration awards, in civil and commercial matters. Consequently, a final judgment by any U.S. federal or state court for payment, whether or not predicated solely upon U.S. federal or state securities laws, would not automatically be enforceable in Germany. In addition, in the past the recognition and enforcement of punitive damages has been denied by German courts as incompatible with the fundamental principles of German law. Moreover, a German court may reduce the amount of damages granted by a U.S. court and recognize damages only to the extent that they are necessary to compensate actual losses or damages. The same considerations regarding enforceability of civil liabilities apply in Sweden.

text:
Denmark: There is doubt as to the enforceability in Denmark of civil liabilities based on U.S. federal or state securities laws, either in an original action or in an action to enforce a judgment obtained in U.S. federal or state courts. The United States and Denmark do not have a treaty providing for reciprocal recognition and enforcement of judgments, other than arbitration awards, in civil and commercial matters, and no executive order has been issued under the Danish Administration of Justice Act (Retsplejeloven) to provide for such recognition and enforcement in relation to the United States. Consequently, a final judgment by any U.S. federal or state court for payment, whether or not predicated solely upon U.S. federal or state securities laws, would not automatically be enforceable in Denmark, although the judgment may be submitted as evidence in a new action before a competent Danish court. Danish law does not recognize punitive or exemplary damages as a form of civil damages, as this is considered contrary to Danish public policy (ordre public), and such awards in actions brought in the United States or elsewhere are unlikely to be enforceable, or otherwise given effect, by Danish courts.
Finland: There is doubt as to the enforceability in Finland of civil liabilities based on U.S. federal or state securities laws, either in an original action or in an action to enforce a judgment obtained in U.S. federal or state courts. The United States and Finland do not have a treaty providing for reciprocal recognition and enforcement of judgments, other than arbitration awards, in civil and commercial matters. Consequently, a final judgment by any U.S. federal or state court for payment, whether or not predicated solely upon U.S. federal or state securities laws, would not automatically be enforceable in Finland, although the judgment may be submitted as evidence in a new action before a competent Finnish court in which case the Finnish court may give such effect to the foreign judgment as it deems appropriate. Finnish law does not recognize punitive or exemplary damages as a form of civil damages, and punitive or exemplary damages may be considered contrary to the fundamental principles of the Finnish legal system. In addition, a Finnish court may reduce the amount of damages granted by a U.S. court and recognize damages only to the extent that they are necessary to compensate actual losses or damages.

text: France: There is doubt as to the enforceability in France of civil liabilities based on U.S. federal or state securities laws, either in an original action or in an action to enforce a judgment of a U.S. court. The United States and France do not have a bilateral treaty providing for the reciprocal recognition and enforcement of judgments (other than arbitral awards) in civil and commercial matters. In the absence of such a treaty, a final and conclusive judgment from a U.S. court is not automatically enforceable in France and requires an enforcement order from a French court. A French court may grant such an order without re-examining the merits of the case, provided it finds that three general conditions are met: (i) the jurisdiction of the U.S. court, which is assessed by determining if the dispute had a “characterized link” with the United States and that French courts did not have exclusive jurisdiction over the matter; (ii) the judgment’s conformity with French international public policy, which includes both substantive and procedural aspects. Regarding substantive public policy, enforcement of a U.S. judgment awarding punitive damages may be denied if the amount is considered disproportionate to the actual loss suffered and the breach of contractual obligations. Procedural public policy essentially consists of principles protecting the fundamental rights of the defense; and (iii) the absence of fraudulent intent to circumvent French law.

text: Ireland: There is currently no treaty in force between Ireland and the United States providing for the automatic, reciprocal recognition and enforcement of judgments (other than arbitration awards) in civil and commercial matters. As a result, a judgment of a U.S. federal or state court would not be automatically enforceable in Ireland, and would instead need to be enforced by means of a fresh action before the Irish courts. Before proceedings may be served on a U.S.-domiciled entity, leave of the Irish courts is required. An applicant must establish a prima facie case and a practical benefit to bringing the proceedings in Ireland. The existence of Irish assets against which the judgment could be enforced is the clearest example of such a benefit. If leave is granted and proceedings are served on the Company, the Irish courts would then consider whether the U.S. judgment should be enforced in accordance with Irish common law principles. Under those principles, an Irish court will generally recognize and enforce a foreign money judgment that is final and conclusive and for a definite sum, provided the foreign court is regarded as having had jurisdiction over the judgment debtor, and provided the judgment is not impeachable on grounds such as fraud, a breach of Irish principles of natural justice, or conflict with Irish public policy or incompatibility with an earlier judgment. There is no assurance that (i) leave would be obtained from the Irish courts to serve proceedings; or (ii) a U.S. civil judgment would satisfy the common law requirements for enforcement in Ireland in any given case.

Switzerland and the United States do not have a treaty providing for reciprocal recognition and enforcement of judgments, other than arbitration awards, in civil and commercial matters. The recognition and enforcement of a judgment of the courts of the United States in Switzerland is governed by the principles set forth in the Swiss Federal Act on Private International Law. This statute provides that the application of provisions of non-Swiss law by the courts in Switzerland shall be precluded if the result is incompatible with Swiss public policy. Also, mandatory provisions of Swiss law may be applicable regardless of any other law that would otherwise apply. The Swiss Federal Act on Private International Law provides in principle that a judgment rendered by a non-Swiss court may be enforced in Switzerland only if: the non-Swiss court had jurisdiction pursuant to the Swiss Federal Act on Private International Law; the judgment of such non-Swiss court has become final and non-appealable; the judgment does not contravene Swiss public policy; the court procedures and the service of documents leading to the judgment were in accordance with the due process of law; and no proceeding involving the same parties and the same subject matter was first brought in Switzerland, or adjudicated in Switzerland, or was earlier adjudicated in a third state and this decision is recognizable in Switzerland.

Our Class F common stock will be voted in the manner provided by the Founder LLC Agreement. Consequently, if the Founder LLC as holder of our single share of Class F common stock exercises its voting rights, the voting power of the holders of our Class A common stock will be limited to 49.9%. For information on the Founder LLC Agreement and the voting mechanics of our Class F common stock, see the sections titled “11.4 Founder LLC Agreement” and “11.5 Class F Common Stock Voting Mechanics.”
We have not provided for cumulative voting for the election of directors in our amended and restated certificate of incorporation.
For information on the voting rights of our other share classes, see “11.2.1.3 Our Capital Stock Following Completion of the Global Offering.”

7.1.5.4 Right to Receive Liquidation Distributions
If we become subject to a liquidation, dissolution, or winding-up, including in bankruptcy, the assets legally available for distribution to our stockholders would be distributable ratably among the holders of our Class A common stock and Class N common stock and any participating preferred stock outstanding at that time, subject to prior satisfaction of all outstanding debt and liabilities and the preferential rights of and the payment of liquidation preferences, if any, on any outstanding shares of our capital stock. In the event of our liquidation, dissolution, or winding-up, including bankruptcy, holders of our Class T common stock, Class F common stock, and Class E common stock shall be entitled to receive par value ($0.00001) per share but shall not otherwise participate in such distributions.

The global offering of our Class A common stock consists of (i) a public offer in the United States, registered under the U.S. Securities Act pursuant to a registration statement on Form S-1 filed with the SEC, referred to as the U.S. offering, (ii) the public offer to retail investors in Germany, Denmark, Finland, France, Ireland, the Netherlands, Norway, Spain and Sweden contemplated by, and on the basis of, this prospectus, referred to as the European retail offering, (iii) the public offer to retail investors in Switzerland contemplated by, and on the basis of, this prospectus, referred to as the Swiss retail offering, (iv) a public offer in Australia, (v) a public offer in certain provinces and territories of Canada, (vi) a public offer in Japan, (vii) a public offer in the United Kingdom, and (viii) private placements (the offerings contemplated under (ii) through (viii) are collectively referred to as the international offering, and together with the U.S. offering are referred to as the global offering).
In the European retail offering, a maximum of 80,135,135 newly issued shares of Class A common stock are offered, referred to as the European retail shares. The global offering initially comprises: (i) 801,351,354 newly issued shares of Class A common stock sold by the Company, including the European retail shares, (ii) up to 23,648,646 existing shares of Class A common stock sold by the selling stockholders identified in section “8.5 Selling Stockholders in the Global Offering” (together referred to as the base shares) and (iii) up to 123,750,000 newly issued shares of Class A common stock which may be sold by the Company to cover potential over-allotments (referred to as the additional shares). The European retail shares form a tranche within the global offering and comprise newly issued shares of Class A common stock of the Company. Any shares offered in the global offering which do not form part of the European retail tranche are offered in any Member State of the EEA solely in circumstances falling within the scope of application of Article 1(4) of the Prospectus Regulation and in Switzerland solely in circumstances falling within the scope of application of Article 36(1) of the FinSA.

8.1.1 Eligible Retail Investors
The European retail offering is solely addressed to individual persons or legal entities which do not qualify as qualified investors within the meaning of Article 2 point (e) of the Prospectus Regulation (referred to as retail investors) and which are resident or located in one of the Covered EEA Countries.
The Prospectus Regulation defines qualified investors as persons or entities that are listed in points (1) to (4) of Section I of Annex II to Directive 2014/65/EU, as amended (“MiFID II”), and persons or entities who are, on request, treated as professional clients in accordance with Section II of that Annex, or recognized as eligible counterparties in accordance with Article 30 of MiFID II unless they have entered into an agreement with their bank or financial intermediary to be treated as non-professional clients in accordance with the fourth paragraph of Section I of that Annex. The Swiss retail offering is solely addressed to individual persons or legal entities which do not qualify as professional clients within the meaning of the FinSA. The FinSA defines “professional clients” as those persons or entities that either (i) are listed in Article 4(3) FinSA and which have not declared an opting-in pursuant to Article 5(5) FinSA or (ii) have requested to be treated as professional client (opting-out) pursuant to Article 5(1) FinSA.
In each case, orders may also be placed by financial intermediaries which act on behalf of retail investors and by financial intermediaries otherwise acting as a fiduciary or agent for one or more investor accounts, where (a) each such account is a retail investor and (b) the financial intermediary has investment discretion with respect to each such account. Investors who have doubts as to whether they meet the eligibility criteria should contact their bank or financial intermediary to verify their client classification with that bank or financial intermediary.

text:
8.1.7 Amendments of the Conditions of the Offering
We reserve the right, after consultation with the representatives, to increase or decrease the total number of offered shares of Class A common stock in the global offering, the European retail offering and the Swiss retail offering, to increase or decrease the maximum public offering price, and/or to extend or shorten the offer period. Changes in relation to the number of offered shares of Class A common stock, changes to the maximum public offering price, or the extension or shortening of the offer period will not invalidate any offers to purchase shares of Class A common stock that have already been submitted. If such change requires the publication of a supplement to the prospectus, investors who submitted purchase orders before the supplement is published shall have the right, pursuant to Article 23 of the Prospectus Regulation, to withdraw these orders to purchase within three working days (within the meaning of Article 2 point (t) of the Prospectus Regulation) of the publication of such supplement, provided that the significant new factor, material mistake or material inaccuracy requiring the publication of a supplement to this prospectus arose or was noted before the closing of the offer period or the delivery of the offered shares of Class A common stock. Investors who have submitted orders to purchase will not be notified individually, except where a financial intermediary is required to notify them under Article 23(3) of the Prospectus Regulation. Instead of withdrawing their orders to purchase our Class A common stock placed prior to the publication of the supplement, investors may change their orders or place new limited or unlimited offers to purchase within three working days (within the meaning of Article 2 point (t) of the Prospectus Regulation) following the publication of the supplement, depending on the procedures of the syndicate banks and financial intermediaries through which orders are placed. Any changes to the terms of the European retail offering, the Swiss retail offering and the global offering will be published on the Company’s website at ipo.anthropic.com, on the SEC’s website at www.sec.gov, and/or, if required, as a supplement to this prospectus.

text:
8.1.9 Termination of the Offering
Upon the occurrence or non-occurrence of certain customary events prior to the expected closing date or the closing date in relation to any additional shares sold pursuant to the option to purchase additional shares described in “8.4.2.2 Option to Purchase Additional Shares” below, the representatives, on behalf of the underwriters, may terminate the underwriting agreement, after the final results of the offering have been determined. Please refer to “8.3.3 Termination and Indemnification” below for further information.
If (i) the global offering is not successful and the underwriting agreement is not executed; or (ii) if the offering is successful and the underwriting agreement is executed but the conditions for the completion of the global offering are not satisfied; or (iii) in case of a termination of the underwriting agreement prior to the expected closing date, then the global offering, including the European retail offering and the Swiss retail offering, will not take place, orders placed for our Class A common stock by investors will be automatically cancelled, allocations of our Class A common stock to investors will become void, and investors will have no claim regarding the delivery of our Class A common stock. Claims with respect to any subscription fees already paid and costs incurred by an investor in connection with the purchase of our Class A common stock will be governed solely by the legal relationship between the investor and the financial intermediary to which the investor submitted its purchase order. The Company and the European underwriters will have no responsibility or liability for orders placed through financial intermediaries other than the European underwriters or for any loss incurred by any person as a result of a termination of the global offering, including the European retail offering and the Swiss retail offering, or the related annulment of any transactions in Class A common stock.

text:
8.1.10 Determination of the Final Results of the Offering Prior to the global offering, there has been no public market for the shares of Class A common stock. The final public offering price and the final number of shares sold will be determined by negotiations among us, the selling stockholders in the global offering, and the representatives of the underwriters. Among the factors considered in determining the final public offering price and the final number of shares sold are prevailing market conditions, our future prospects and those of our industry in general, our historical financial and operating performance in recent periods, an assessment by our management and the consideration of the above factors in relation to market valuation of companies engaged in activities similar to ours.
8.1.11 Publication of the Final Results of the Offering The results of the global offering, the European retail offering and the Swiss retail offering are expected to be published on or about November 18, 2026, by means of a notice to be published in electronic form on the Company’s website at ipo.anthropic.com.
Investors who have placed purchase orders with one of the European underwriters, the Swiss underwriter or financial intermediaries can obtain information from that underwriter or financial intermediary about the final public offering price and the number of shares of Class A common stock allotted to them following the pricing. As trading in the Company’s shares on the Nasdaq Global Select Market is expected to begin on or about November 19, 2026, investors may not have obtained information about the number of shares allotted to them at the time of beginning of trading.

text:
8.2.1 Plan of Allotment
The global offering of the shares of Class A common stock by the underwriters is subject to receipt and acceptance and subject to the underwriters’ right to reject any order in whole or in part, at their discretion. Such discretionary allocation may result in financial intermediaries receiving allocations that differ from one another, and each financial intermediary may apply its own allocation principles when allocating shares of Class A common stock to its clients. As a result, the allocations received by retail investors participating in the European retail offering and the Swiss retail offering may differ.
European retail offering and Swiss retail offering – The European retail shares offered in the European retail offering and the Swiss retail offering form a tranche within the global offering. If and to the extent the European retail shares are not subscribed for by retail investors or if the Company and the European underwriters decide to reduce the number of offered European retail shares or set a final amount of European retail shares offered below the maximum number of shares offered under this prospectus, the European retail shares not subscribed for or no longer offered under this prospectus, respectively, may be offered and sold in the global offering, provided that in any Member State of the EEA they will be offered solely in circumstances falling within the scope of application of Article 1(4) of the Prospectus Regulation and in Switzerland solely in circumstances falling within the scope of application of Article 36(1) of the FinSA.

8.2.3 MiFID Product Governance Requirements
Solely for the purposes of the product governance requirements contained within: (i) MiFID II; (ii) Articles 9 and 10 of Commission Delegated Directive (EU) 2017/593 supplementing MiFID II; and (iii) local implementing measures (together, the “MiFID II Product Governance Requirements”), and without assuming any responsibility or liability, whether arising in tort, contract or otherwise, which any “manufacturer” (for the purposes of the MiFID II Product Governance Requirements) may otherwise have with respect thereto, the Class A common stock has been subject to a product approval process, which has determined that such Class A common stock is: (i) compatible with an end target market of retail investors and investors who meet the criteria of professional clients and eligible counterparties, each as defined in MiFID II; and (ii) eligible for distribution through all distribution channels as are permitted by MiFID II (the “Target Market Assessment”).

text: Notwithstanding the Target Market Assessment, the price of the Class A common stock may decline and investors could lose all or part of their investment; the Class A common stock offers no guaranteed income and no capital protection; and an investment in the Class A common stock is suitable only for investors who do not need a guaranteed income or capital protection, who have at least informed knowledge and experience with financial instruments and (either alone or in conjunction with an appropriate financial or other adviser) are capable of evaluating the merits and risks of such an investment, and who have sufficient resources to be able to bear any losses that may result therefrom. The Target Market Assessment is without prejudice to the requirements of any contractual, legal, or regulatory selling restrictions in relation to the European retail offering. Furthermore, it is noted that, notwithstanding the Target Market Assessment, the underwriters will only procure investors who meet the criteria of professional clients and eligible counterparties in the private placement parts of the global offering. For the avoidance of doubt, the Target Market Assessment does not constitute: (i) an assessment of suitability or appropriateness for the purposes of MiFID II or (ii) a recommendation to any investor or group of investors to invest in, or purchase, or take any other action whatsoever with respect to, the Class A common stock. Each distributor is responsible for undertaking its own Target Market Assessment in respect of the Class A common stock and determining appropriate distribution channels.

text:
8.4.2.1 Stabilization Transactions
In order to facilitate the offering of our Class A common stock, Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC, acting as stabilization agent on behalf of the underwriters, may engage in transactions that stabilize, maintain, or otherwise affect the price of our Class A common stock. Specifically, the underwriter may sell more shares of Class A common stock than the underwriters are obligated to purchase under the underwriting agreement, creating a short position. A short sale is covered if the short position is no greater than the number of shares available for purchase under the underwriters’ option to purchase additional shares set forth in section “8.4.2.2 Option to Purchase Additional Shares.” The underwriter can close out a covered short sale by exercising the underwriters’ option to purchase additional shares or purchasing shares in the open market. In determining the source of shares to close out a covered short sale, the underwriter will consider, among other things, the open market price of our Class A common stock compared to the price available under the underwriters’ option to purchase additional shares. The underwriter may also sell shares of Class A common stock in excess of the underwriters’ option to purchase additional shares, creating a naked short position. The underwriter must close out any naked short position by purchasing shares of Class A common stock in the open market. A naked short position is more likely to be created if the underwriter is concerned that there may be downward pressure on the price of our Class A common stock in the open market after pricing that could adversely affect investors who purchase shares of Class A common stock in the global offering. As an additional means of facilitating the global offering, the underwriter may bid for, and purchase, shares of Class A common stock in the open market to stabilize the price of our Class A common stock. These activities may raise or maintain the market price of our Class A common stock above independent market levels or prevent or slow a decline in the market price of our Class A common stock. The underwriter is not required to engage in these activities and may end any of these activities at any time.
The underwriters may offer and sell the shares of common stock through certain of their affiliates or other registered broker-dealers or selling agents.

8.8.2 Economic Dilution of Existing and New Shareholders
If you invest in our Class A common stock in the global offering, your ownership interest will be diluted to the extent of the difference between the initial public offering price per share of our Class A common stock and the as further adjusted net tangible book value per share of our Class A common stock and Class N common stock immediately after the global offering and the concurrent private placement. Net tangible book value dilution per share to new investors represents the difference between the amount per share paid by purchasers of shares of our Class A common stock in the global offering and the as further adjusted net tangible book value per share of our Class A common stock and Class N common stock immediately after completion of the global offering and the concurrent private placement.

5.1 Definitions. For purposes of this Amended and Restated Certificate, the following definitions apply:
(a) “Acquisition” means (A) any consolidation or merger of the Corporation with or into any other corporation or other entity or person, or any other corporate reorganization, other than any such consolidation, merger or reorganization in which the shares of capital stock of the Corporation immediately prior to such consolidation, merger or reorganization continue to represent a majority of the voting power of the surviving entity (or, if the surviving entity is a wholly owned subsidiary, its parent) immediately after such consolidation, merger or reorganization (provided that, for the purpose of this ARTICLE V, Section 5.1, all stock, options, warrants, purchase rights or other securities exercisable for or convertible into Participating Common Stock outstanding immediately prior to such consolidation, merger or reorganization shall be deemed to be outstanding immediately prior to such consolidation, merger or reorganization and, if applicable, converted or exchanged in such consolidation, merger or reorganization on the same terms as the actual outstanding shares of capital stock are converted or exchanged); or (B) any transaction or series of related transactions to which the Corporation is a party in which shares of the Corporation are transferred such that in excess of fifty percent (50%) of the outstanding shares of Participating Common Stock are transferred; provided that an Acquisition shall not include (i) any redemption or forfeiture pursuant to Sections 5.3(b), 5.4(b) or 5.5(b) of ARTICLE V below, or (ii) any transaction or series of transactions principally for bona fide equity financing purposes in which cash is received by the Corporation or any successor or indebtedness of the Corporation is cancelled or converted or a combination thereof.
(b) “Affiliate” means any person or entity that, directly or indirectly through one or more intermediaries, controls or is controlled by or is under common control with a person or entity, as such terms are used in and construed under Rule 405 under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended.
(c) “Amended and Restated Certificate” means this Amended and Restated Certificate of Incorporation, as may be further amended and restated from time to time.
(d) “Asset Transfer” means a sale, lease, exclusive license or other disposition of all or substantially all of the assets of the Corporation.
(e) “Board” means the Board of Directors of the Corporation.

text: (f) “Cause” means, with respect to the termination of the status of a holder of Class E Common Stock as a Service Provider, (A) any material breach by the holder of any material written agreement between the holder and the Corporation and the holder’s failure to cure such breach within thirty (30) calendar days after receiving written notice thereof, that results in, or is reasonably expected to result in, material harm to the business or reputation of the Corporation; (B) any failure by the holder to comply with the Corporation’s material written policies or rules as they may be in effect from time to time that results in, or is reasonably expected to result in, material harm to the business or reputation of the Corporation; (C) the holder’s repeated failure to follow reasonable and lawful instructions from the Board, the Corporation’s Chief Executive Officer or the holder’s direct supervisor(s) and the holder’s failure to cure such condition within thirty (30) calendar days after receiving written notice thereof; (D) the holder’s conviction of, or plea of guilty or nolo contendere to, any crime that results in, or is reasonably expected to result in, material harm to the business or reputation of the Corporation; (E) the holder’s commission of or participation in an act of fraud against the Corporation; (F) the holder’s intentional material damage to the Corporation’s business, property or reputation; or (G) the holder’s unauthorized use or disclosure of any proprietary information or trade secrets of the Corporation or any other party to whom the holder owes an obligation of nondisclosure as a result of their relationship with the Corporation. The determination as to whether the holder’s status as a Service Provider for purposes of ARTICLE V, Section 5.3(b) has been terminated for Cause shall be made in good faith by the Corporation and shall be final and binding on the holder. For purposes of this definition of Cause, the term “Corporation” will be interpreted to include any Affiliate (including the holder of the Class T Common Stock then outstanding), or any successor thereto, if appropriate.

5.2 Rights of Participating Common Stock.
(a) Identical Rights. Except as otherwise provided in this Amended and Restated Certificate or required by applicable law, shares of Participating Common Stock shall have the same rights and powers, rank equally (including as to dividends and distributions, and any liquidation, dissolution or winding up of the Corporation but excluding voting and other matters as described in ARTICLE V, Section 5.6 below), share ratably and be identical in all respects as to all matters, including:
(i) Subject to the prior rights of holders of all classes and series of stock at the time outstanding having prior rights as to dividends, the holders of Participating Common Stock shall be entitled to receive, when, as and if declared by the Board, out of any assets of the Corporation legally available therefor, such dividends as may be declared from time to time by the Board. Any dividends paid to the holders of shares of Participating Common Stock shall be paid pro rata, on an equal priority, pari passu basis, unless different treatment of the shares of any such series is approved by the affirmative vote of the holders of a majority of the voting power of the outstanding shares of such applicable series of Participating Common Stock treated adversely, voting separately as a series.
